a3.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3.name: Donald Trump
a3.title: US President
a3.speech: One of the conditions for resuming aid is that "the foreign aid industry and bureaucracy" must be "aligned with American interests" ; according to the Trump doctrine, the way American aid is currently carried out is "contrary to American values and serves to destabilize world peace by promoting ideas in foreign countries that are directly opposed to harmonious and stable relations within and between countries" ; declared that "no additional US foreign aid will be disbursed in a manner that is not fully consistent with the foreign policy of the President of the United States."

a3.speaker: US Embassy in Guinea
a3.name: US Embassy in Guinea
a3.speech: According to the Embassy, the United States' financial commitment amounts to more than one billion dollars for 2024, most of which goes to the Boké liquefied gas project and the purchase of locomotives for the Simandou project by American companies.

a3.speaker: Andy Ogles, US Representative (Tennessee)
a3.name: Andy Ogles
a3.title: US Representative (Tennessee)
a3.speech: "[Trump] has proven that he is the only figure in modern history capable of reversing our nation's decline and restoring America's greatness, and he must be given the time necessary to achieve this goal," declared while proposing a resolution to amend the US Constitution to allow Trump to be elected for a third term.

a11.speaker: US Embassy in Maputo (press statement)
a11.name: US Embassy in Maputo (press statement)
a11.speech: Announced that the MCC Board of Directors decided to continue the Compact program in Mozambique, budgeted at $500 million ; "The MCC Board of Directors met in August and recommended moving forward with Mozambique's Connectivity and Coastal Resilience Compact" ; the recommendation "reflects continued confidence in US-Mozambique cooperation, highlighting the commitment to generate tangible results for both peoples" ; the program "is fully aligned with US foreign policy priorities" and "aims to produce concrete benefits" for both peoples ; the development underscores the US government's commitment to accountability, transparency, and measurable results, ensuring taxpayer investment promotes mutual prosperity.

a11.speaker: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a11.name: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a11.speech: Confided to the newspaper that the continuation of cooperation between the MCC and the Mozambican government is the result of the "insight" of the discreet diplomacy developed by Mozambique's head of state, Daniel Chapo, "which required consideration of very high-level engagements."

a457.speaker: Hospital source contacted on the spot (anonymous)
a457.name: Hospital source contacted on the spot (anonymous)
a457.speech: “The tragedy occurred between the districts of Boukaria and Kourouda, in a mine worked in an artisanal manner” ; according to the same source, the victims number eight and were aged from 1 to 6 years.

a485.speaker: Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug, Mauritanian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Mauritanians Abroad
a485.name: Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug
a485.title: Mauritanian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Mauritanians Abroad
a485.speech: "The two heads of state have this shared desire to consolidate, diversify and strengthen this relationship in the interest of the two peoples and for the benefit of the whole sub-region" ; expressed his satisfaction at having a perfect identity of views with the Malian side on all the questions addressed.

a485.speaker: Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug, Mauritanian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Mauritanians Abroad
a485.name: Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug
a485.title: Mauritanian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Mauritanians Abroad
a485.speech: Recalled that the majority of African migratory movements take place within the continent: "80% of African migrants remain in Africa, within the framework of traditional migrations that are often beneficial to local economies and to social cohesion" ; expressed his keen concern at the worrying rise of irregular immigration orchestrated by human trafficking networks: "In 2024, more than 500 bodies of young Africans were recovered off our coasts, and more than 100 since the beginning of this year. It is a human tragedy that we must confront together" ; insisted on the need for a coordinated and anticipatory response based on cooperation between states: "It is imperative to combat these criminal networks and to encourage regular, safe and orderly migration, in strict respect of national legislation and bilateral agreements."

a485.speaker: Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug, Mauritanian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Mauritanians Abroad
a485.name: Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug
a485.title: Mauritanian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Mauritanians Abroad
a485.speech: Reaffirmed the fraternal and hospitable character of relations between the two peoples regarding Malian nationals living in Mauritania: "A Malian who arrives in Mauritania is at home, just as a Mauritanian who goes to Mali is. Those who are in a regular situation live in complete peace. The difficulties mainly concern unregistered persons, which requires better organisation on both sides" ; "What we ask of people is to ensure that what we are preparing together is respected."

a485.speaker: Communique of the Malian presidency
a485.name: Communique of the Malian presidency
a485.speech: States that the exchange "made it possible to address questions of common interest, notably the strengthening of bilateral cooperation and the concerted management of migratory flows."

a485.speaker: Mohamed Ould El-Ghazaouani, President of Mauritania
a485.name: Mohamed Ould El-Ghazaouani
a485.title: President of Mauritania
a485.speech: Sent a message to the President of the Transition, Army General Assimi Goita, carried by his Minister of Foreign Affairs.

a633.speaker: Hirut W. Mariayam, Ministry of Higher Education and Science (Ethiopia)
a633.name: Hirut W. Mariayam
a633.title: Ministry of Higher Education and Science (Ethiopia)
a633.speech: “The initiative helps our country to have competitive graduates in the market in compliance with the 15-year education road map to ensure quality education and jobs.”

a633.speaker: Sonjai Reynolds-Cooper, Director of USAID's Education and Youth office
a633.name: Sonjai Reynolds-Cooper
a633.title: Director of USAID's Education and Youth office
a633.speech: “We believe investing in education is one of the best investments we can all make as this initiative will support Ethiopia's Journey to self-reliance in line with the country's education system reform.”

a689.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President (decree)
a689.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a689.title: Ukrainian President (decree)
a689.speech: Signed a decree, this Sunday, imposing sanctions on 94 people and five legal entities, under a proposal from the Security Service of Ukraine, covering people from eight countries — Russia, Iran, Pakistan, China, Myanmar, Bangladesh, India and Georgia — and resulting in the deprivation of state concessions, freezing of assets, restrictions on commercial transactions, prevention of capital withdrawal and suspension of economic and financial obligations.

a689.speaker: Security Service of Ukraine
a689.name: Security Service of Ukraine
a689.speech: Proposed the sanctions that were imposed by the presidential decree.

a735.speaker: Ministry of Information, Culture, and Tourism of the Federal Government of Somalia (press statement)
a735.name: Ministry of Information
a735.title: Culture, and Tourism of the Federal Government of Somalia (press statement)
a735.speech: Expresses deep regret over the consequences of the ongoing clan conflicts in various regions of the country; said it is closely monitoring social media platforms and media outlets being misused to fuel conflicts by individuals contributing to the incitement of violence; said the dissemination of videos, images, audio recordings, and distressing or inflammatory texts that exacerbate conflicts is prohibited under Islamic law, national laws, international regulations, and the policies of social media companies.

a735.speaker: Ministry of Information, Culture, and Tourism of the Federal Government of Somalia (press statement)
a735.name: Ministry of Information
a735.title: Culture, and Tourism of the Federal Government of Somalia (press statement)
a735.speech: Issues a warning to social media users engaging in creating unrest and inciting violence, stating that the government will take legal action to restrict any individual or platform used to escalate clan conflicts; said every citizen today bears the responsibility of preventing the fueling of conflicts and working towards peace; urged the Somali public to report platforms inciting violence to the Ministry by email.

a735.speaker: Ministry of Information, Culture, and Tourism of the Federal Government of Somalia (press statement)
a735.name: Ministry of Information
a735.title: Culture, and Tourism of the Federal Government of Somalia (press statement)
a735.speech: Appreciates the media outlets and social media users who are spreading positive and awareness-raising messages, as they set the good example needed today; said national law enforcement agencies, led by the police and the Attorney General's Office, are on high alert to take appropriate measures during this period.

a821.speaker: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report, published in The Lancet
a821.name: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report
a821.title: published in The Lancet
a821.speech: Reveals that the global mortality rate has declined by 67 per cent since 1950, despite population growth and ageing; reports that global life expectancy has returned to pre-pandemic levels, rising by more than 20 years since 1950 to 76.3 years for females and 71.5 years for males, and highlights wide regional disparities, with life expectancy ranging from as high as 83 years in high-income regions to as low as 62 years in sub-Saharan Africa.

a821.speaker: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report, published in The Lancet
a821.name: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report
a821.title: published in The Lancet
a821.speech: Warned of an emerging crisis of higher death rates among adolescents and young adults, attributing the rise to suicide and substance use in North and Latin America and to infectious diseases and unintentional injuries in sub-Saharan Africa; said that between 2011 and 2023 the highest increase in deaths was recorded among those aged 20 to 39 in high-income North America, largely due to suicide, drug overdose and excessive alcohol use, and noted that deaths among those aged five to 19 rose in Eastern Europe, high-income North America and the Caribbean.

a821.speaker: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report, published in The Lancet
a821.name: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report
a821.title: published in The Lancet
a821.speech: “The all-cause probability of dying before age 70 decreased across each GBD super-region and region from 2000 to 2023, with drug use disorders as one of the leading causes. In sub-Saharan Africa, the probability increased for many Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD), and the mean age of death from NCDs was lower than expected.”

a821.speaker: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report, published in The Lancet
a821.name: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report
a821.title: published in The Lancet
a821.speech: Noted that tremendous progress has been made in slashing many infectious diseases and injuries and improving the health of newborns, but that cuts to development assistance for health threaten this success.

a821.speaker: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report, published in The Lancet
a821.name: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report
a821.title: published in The Lancet
a821.speech: Revealed that new data and methods uncovered higher mortality among girls and women aged 15–29 in sub-Saharan Africa, 61 per cent greater than previously reported, mainly due to maternal mortality, road injuries and meningitis, and that more children aged five to 14 in sub-Saharan Africa died between 1950 and 2021 than earlier estimates showed; stated that many countries, particularly those with the fewest resources, need better access to prevention and treatment for non-communicable diseases.

a821.speaker: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report, published in The Lancet
a821.name: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) report
a821.title: published in The Lancet
a821.speech: Stated that NCDs account for nearly two-thirds of the world’s total death and disability, led by ischemic heart disease, stroke and diabetes; that half of the world’s disease burden was preventable and driven by 88 modifiable risks, with the top three being high blood pressure, air pollution and smoking; and that the burden of mental disorders continued to surge globally, with anxiety and depression increasing death and disability by 63 per cent and 26 per cent respectively.

a821.speaker: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a821.name: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a821.speech: Reports that the findings were presented and unveiled at the ongoing World Health Summit in Berlin, Germany, from 12 October to 14 October, and that the study was led by Christopher Murray, Director of the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington School of Medicine, alongside its GBD Collaborator Network.

a824.speaker: UNOPS (statement)
a824.name: UNOPS (statement)
a824.speech: Announced that Executive Director Mr. Moreira da Silva will visit Ethiopia, Somalia and Sudan from 13 to 17 April, and that during his visit he will meet national authorities and development partners and discuss the practical solutions that UNOPS offers to partners to maximize the impact of their humanitarian, development and peace operations ― all in support of the Sustainable Development Goals; said the visit also aims at getting a better understanding of the needs on the ground, and how UNOPS can scale operations to respond.

a824.speaker: UNOPS (statement)
a824.name: UNOPS (statement)
a824.speech: Stated that in Sudan, where half of the population ― some 25 million people ― need humanitarian assistance and protection, UNOPS is strengthening health infrastructure, improving access to clean, safe water, supporting peacekeeping operations to protect civilians, and facilitating a more sustainable and equitable use of natural resources; that in Somalia, UNOPS works to strengthen the capacity of Somali institutions and supports partners in sectors such as health, governance, peace and security, including reconstruction and state-building through disaster preparedness planning, crisis recovery, climate-resilient infrastructure and strengthening of the security sector; and that in Ethiopia, UNOPS works with partners to support national and international development priorities, having helped strengthen health and education systems and supported food security.

a862.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice-President of Tanzania
a862.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a862.title: Vice-President of Tanzania
a862.speech: Noted that poor road infrastructure contributes to 16 per cent to road crashes and warned that without effective measures, serious road crashes could become the leading cause of death by 2030 ; When launching the road safety initiative in August, he highlighted the troubling 13.3 per cent rise in motorcyclist fatalities nationwide – 376 deaths during January to December 2023, up from 332 in the same period in 2022.

a862.speaker: Police statistics (Tanzania)
a862.name: Police statistics (Tanzania)
a862.speech: According to police statistics, there were 1,733 road crashes in 2023, up from 1,720 in 2022; deaths from these crashes totalled 1,647 in 2023, marking a 6.6 per cent increase from the 1,545 deaths reported in 2022, and injuries rose to 2,716 in 2023 from 2,278 in 2022.

a886.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a886.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a886.speech: Warned on Tuesday that millions of people are at risk of hunger as southern Africa enters the lean season, and appealed for urgent assistance in southern Africa to prevent widespread drought triggered by the El Niño phenomenon from becoming a “full-blown humanitarian catastrophe.”

a886.speaker: World Food Programme (UN agency)
a886.name: World Food Programme (UN agency)
a886.speech: According to the UN agency, five southern African countries – Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe – have all declared the hunger crisis a catastrophe, requesting international humanitarian assistance, while Angola and Mozambique are also badly affected ; according to WFP, harvests fell short of farmers’ expectations, while livestock have perished and children are lucky to receive even one meal a day ; WFP says it has begun providing food assistance and essential support for transport, logistics and food procurement at the request of governments, and plans to scale up seasonal relief operations to more than 6.5 million people in the seven hardest-hit countries through March 2025.

a886.speaker: Tomson Phiri, WFP spokesperson for southern Africa
a886.name: Tomson Phiri
a886.title: WFP spokesperson for southern Africa
a886.speech: “October marks the beginning of the lean season and each month is expected to be worse than the previous one until the next harvest in March/April” ; “The situation is dire and the need for action has never been clearer,” noting that more than 6.5 million people are in need of assistance in the seven countries.

a886.speaker: Tomson Phiri, WFP spokesperson for southern Africa
a886.name: Tomson Phiri
a886.title: WFP spokesperson for southern Africa
a886.speech: Warned: “If we do not receive additional resources, millions of people risk going through the worst lean season in decades without assistance,” calling for massive funding to carry out the planned actions.

a1062.speaker: Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a1062.name: Isaias Afwerki
a1062.title: President of Eritrea
a1062.speech: Referring to the letter the Ethiopian government is said to have written to the United Nations, indicated that the letter was written in order to level false accusations against Eritrea, and said it was done by the Ethiopian government to cover up its own war preparations. He said the reason Ethiopia, instead of returning to peace after the Pretoria peace agreement, went back to war and fell into tension is that the Ethiopian government did not want to implement the peace agreement in good faith and because it opened an unnecessary war against Fano forces. He also accused the Ethiopian government of preparing to open another round of war against Eritrea instead of focusing on resolving the great turmoil inside Ethiopia.

a1062.speaker: Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a1062.name: Isaias Afwerki
a1062.title: President of Eritrea
a1062.speech: Asked in his recent interview, "Why was it necessary to open war against Fano forces in the aftermath of Pretoria?" and voiced the position, "Why is Pretoria not being properly implemented?"

a1062.speaker: Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea (interview of Hidar 2017 E.C. / November 2024)
a1062.name: Isaias Afwerki
a1062.title: President of Eritrea (interview of Hidar 2017 E.C. / November 2024)
a1062.speech: "The Pretoria agreement does not concern us. The Pretoria agreement was made to stop the war. Stopping war is in itself a good thing. The agreement does not worry us; we have no reason either to support it or to oppose it. Had the Pretoria peace agreement been properly implemented, the complicated problem that exists now would not have arisen." ; At that time he said the Pretoria agreement was drafted and presented by foreign forces, and said indirectly that the agreement had achieved more or less nothing for peace; he criticised the Ethiopian government for declaring war in the aftermath of the agreement insisting on disarming Fano, and was heard saying that after Pretoria the main source of instability inside Ethiopia and in the region was his former friend and current enemy, the Ethiopian government.

a1062.speaker: Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a1062.name: Isaias Afwerki
a1062.title: President of Eritrea
a1062.speech: Said that the Ethiopian government, emboldened by the support and encouragement of the United States, France and principally the United Arab Emirates, is creating problems for Eritrea and for the region, and was heard saying "let the Ethiopian people and the whole world be our witness": "We are not afraid; we are not alarmed by the Ethiopian government's arms build-up or its threats. While the Ethiopian government is engaged in arms purchases and creating provocative acts, there is no reason whatsoever for us to be accused of being the guilty party. The world is coming to understand that the dangerous move of the Ethiopian government, which says it must obtain sovereign sea access, is destabilising the region, and it is known that there is pressure from foreign forces behind it."

a1062.speaker: Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a1062.name: Isaias Afwerki
a1062.title: President of Eritrea
a1062.speech: Said that the Ethiopian government, in order to please foreign powers and with a plan to harm the government of Djibouti, asked the Eritrean government to let it make Assab its main export and import trade corridor port, and that the Ethiopian government had the idea of leaving Djibouti's port idle and without traffic by diverting its export-import trade to Assab, drying up the four billion dollars a year Djibouti earns. "We responded by telling them that Eritrea would not be a collaborator in this malicious agenda of the Ethiopian government and that it does not want any neighbour to be harmed," adding that even now the sea-access agreement Ethiopia made with Somaliland is one that divides the region and creates tension.

a1062.speaker: Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a1062.name: Isaias Afwerki
a1062.title: President of Eritrea
a1062.speech: Said that the fighting the Ethiopian government is waging with Fano is unnecessary and that going into tension with the TPLF is also not appropriate; however, he presented the new relationship with the TPLF, called "Tsimdo", as necessary even for regional peace, and said he has no desire to go to war unless compelled to do so.

a1062.speaker: Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea (interview of Hidar 2017 E.C. / November 2024)
a1062.name: Isaias Afwerki
a1062.title: President of Eritrea (interview of Hidar 2017 E.C. / November 2024)
a1062.speech: Was heard saying that the diplomatic tension between Somalia and Ethiopia had put the region at risk, while arguing that the tripartite cooperation Eritrea made with Egypt and Somalia does not harm Ethiopia's interests: "Both the Egyptians and the Somalis have their own positions. But the matters we meet and discuss with them are not ones that push the region into confrontation, and they have nothing to do with Ethiopia. At this time when Ethiopia's internal problems have worsened, there is no relationship being created in order to further complicate Ethiopia's problems. But as long as there is a worrying situation in Ethiopia, since it concerns all of us, there may be discussion among us about how to resolve it."

a1062.speaker: Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a1062.name: Isaias Afwerki
a1062.title: President of Eritrea
a1062.speech: "Under no circumstances will we enter into a war with a neighbouring country at the desire of the Eritrean government. But we are ready to repel any war that is opened against us."

a1062.speaker: Biniam Assefa, author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity" posted on the website of the Ethiopian Institute of Foreign Affairs
a1062.name: Biniam Assefa
a1062.title: author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity" posted on the website of the Ethiopian Institute of Foreign Affairs
a1062.speech: Describes as a fundamental matter "the periodic change in the character of the historical relationship between the TPLF and Shaebia that began from the struggle in the bush"; narrates that after the fall of the Derg, Shaebia and the TPLF, which held the highest political power in the two countries, had a relationship that cooled at one time and warmed at another, and reviews that this is what drove the two countries into a border war over Badme and created the years of confrontation thereafter; details that after political change came in Ethiopia and Abiy Ahmed (PhD) came to power, Ethiopia reconciled with Eritrea, agreements were signed and efforts were made to strengthen the relationship.

a1062.speaker: Biniam Assefa, author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.name: Biniam Assefa
a1062.title: author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.speech: "The outbreak of the northern war was a test of Ethiopia-Eritrea relations. The government's following the path of peace to conclude the war did not please them. Shaebia mainly wanted the war to continue until the TPLF was destroyed."

a1062.speaker: Biniam Assefa, author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.name: Biniam Assefa
a1062.title: author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.speech: Explains that when Ethiopia began raising the sea-access question the relations of the two countries began to deteriorate further; reviews that Ethiopia long had sea access on the Red Sea beginning with the ports of Adulis and Massawa, and calls Ethiopia's having remained without sea access after Eritrea's independence a historical mistake. "Because Ethiopia lost its sea access, it has lived as a vulnerable country whose security is threatened by forces within and outside the region" - adding that the Eritrean elites are now viewing the question Ethiopia has raised with suspicion and as a threat, the source of which is the Eritrean elites' viewing of Ethiopia as a coloniser.

a1062.speaker: Biniam Assefa, author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.name: Biniam Assefa
a1062.title: author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.speech: Using the saying "War is not only part of the cycle of change of nations; nations are also built and come to be broken through war," or "Warfare is Part of State Development, State Making, As well As State Breaking," argues, by establishing that Eritrea too became a country in this same way, that there is no possibility for Ethiopia to be seen as a coloniser; also uses Charles Tilly's expression "War Makes the State and the State Makes War", indicating that the history of Eritrea and Ethiopia cannot be seen apart from this cycle of war.

a1062.speaker: Biniam Assefa, author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.name: Biniam Assefa
a1062.title: author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.speech: "The Eritrean elites think their country is a completely different country from Ethiopia. They also think Ethiopia is a threat to our existence. They are also heard saying Ethiopia is a threat to our independence. But the two countries, which have about a 1,033-kilometre common border, are inseparable and united not only geographically but in culture, language, faith, history and many social interactions."

a1062.speaker: Biniam Assefa, author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.name: Biniam Assefa
a1062.title: author of the article "Unending Relations: Ethiopia and Eritrea Between Amity and Enmity"
a1062.speech: "When the federal government decided that the northern Ethiopia war should end, it also invited Eritrea to come to the peace forum. But the Eritrean government did not accept. It failed because it said it did not want it unless the TPLF was destroyed. They said they did not want to sign a document drafted by the Washingtonians and that the African Union is a puppet. Now, worse still, the Eritrean government supplies arms and intelligence support to Amhara and TPLF forces. It scrambles to gain ideological and geopolitical advantage in the region. It conspires with Ethiopia's enemies to sacrifice Ethiopia. It links the sea-access agenda with Nile politics and carries out anti-Ethiopia activity. The creation of an Eritrea-Egypt-Somalia front is an attempt to endanger Ethiopia's security."

a1062.speaker: Political analyst who did not want his name mentioned (anonymous)
a1062.name: Political analyst who did not want his name mentioned (anonymous)
a1062.speech: "The new thing I found in President Isaias's speech is the place where he said we want to soften and correct our relations with America and Israel. In my view, this is where Eritrea clearly showed a position that it wants to become a friend of America and the like. The Americans too will now start calculating that making anyone a friend would be the better choice. In particular, they will think carefully about which of Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia or Somalia would help them with the plan they have to take the Palestinians of Gaza to another place and settle them. From the information I have, I know that the Houthis holed up in Yemen, aided by intelligence from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard security section, carry out attacks on ships passing through the Red Sea. To counter the Houthis, who are Iran's proxy weapon, the Westerners want to find one partner convenient to them in the Horn of Africa."

a1062.speaker: Political analyst who did not want his name mentioned (anonymous)
a1062.name: Political analyst who did not want his name mentioned (anonymous)
a1062.speech: Notes that Isaias Afwerki is now supported by Saudi Arabia and others, as well as by Egypt, because of the role he played in the Sudan war; said that in order to withstand the pressure and threat Isaias says he faces from the Ethiopian side, Isaias wants not only Russia and China but even Washington to line up as allies and is making efforts to achieve this. According to him, for the Ethiopia-Eritrea tension to move beyond proxy skirmishes and conflict involving the TPLF, Brigade N'Hamedu, the Red Sea Afar Liberation front and other regional actors into full war, it will necessarily await the war-starting whistle of the great powers; he gave his estimate that no one will go to war without securely obtaining the support and permission of the Westerners or the Arabs.

a1335.speaker: UN World Health Organization (WHO)
a1335.name: UN World Health Organization (WHO)
a1335.speech: Said that eight countries - six of them in Africa, including Nigeria, Kenya and Lesotho - could soon run out of HIV drugs following the US government's recent decision to pause foreign aid.

a1335.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief
a1335.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a1335.title: WHO chief
a1335.speech: Warned that "Disruptions to HIV programmes could undo 20 years of progress," adding that it could also lead to more than 10 million additional cases of HIV and three million HIV-related deaths, noting this was "more than triple the number of deaths last year."

a1335.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief
a1335.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a1335.title: WHO chief
a1335.speech: Said at a press conference on Monday that Nigeria, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso and Mali - as well as Haiti and Ukraine - would run out of life-saving anti-retroviral (ARV) medicines in the coming months.

a1335.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief
a1335.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a1335.title: WHO chief
a1335.speech: Said the aid pause has led to the "immediate stop to services for HIV treatment, testing and prevention in more than 50 countries."

a1335.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief
a1335.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a1335.title: WHO chief
a1335.speech: "The US administration has been extremely generous over many years. And of course, it's within its rights to decide what it supports and to what extent," ; "But the US also has a responsibility to ensure that if it withdraws direct funding for countries, it's done in an orderly and humane way that allows them to find alternative sources of funding." ; "We ask the US to reconsider its support for global health, which not only saves lives around the world, it also makes the US safer by preventing outbreaks from spreading internationally."

a1335.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1335.name: Donald Trump
a1335.title: US President
a1335.speech: Announced the freeze on foreign aid on his first day in office in January as part of a review into government spending, and also announced during his first days in office that the US would pull out of the WHO.

a1335.speaker: WHO data
a1335.name: WHO data
a1335.speech: Kenya has the seventh-largest number of people living with HIV in the world, at around 1.4 million, according to WHO data.

a1336.speaker: Joseph Hamilton, Charge d'affaires of the Embassy of the United States of America in Djibouti
a1336.name: Joseph Hamilton
a1336.title: Charge d'affaires of the Embassy of the United States of America in Djibouti
a1336.speech: Noted in his speech his expectations for the end of the three-day workshop, stating: "Participants will also be equipped with tools enabling them to adopt best practices for integrating gender and social inclusion into their work, thereby aligning themselves with the 'Djibouti Vision 2035' of the Head of State, President Guelleh, for access to basic education for all in the transformation of the school for better quality learning."

a1484.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, Zimbabwean President and SADC Chairperson
a1484.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
a1484.title: Zimbabwean President and SADC Chairperson
a1484.speech: Warned that the ripple effects of the conflict extend beyond the DRC, posing a significant security threat to the broader region. “Our shared goal is to see a secure and prosperous DRC,” Mnangagwa said in his opening remarks. “The review of the SAMIDRC [SADC Mission in the DRC] mandate that is expected of this meeting is, therefore, timely, the outcome of which must contribute to the attainment of peace and stability in eastern DRC and ultimately, the entire region.”

a1484.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a1484.name: Elias Magosi
a1484.title: SADC Executive Secretary
a1484.speech: Described the situation as “worrisome,” noting that the violence has led to a sharp increase in internally displaced persons, particularly among vulnerable populations such as women, children and the elderly. Magosi condemned the rebel attacks, calling them “unwarranted,” and reaffirmed SADC’s commitment to standing in solidarity with the DRC.

a1484.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a1484.name: Elias Magosi
a1484.title: SADC Executive Secretary
a1484.speech: “The situation is compounded by the blockade of main supply routes and the capture by the M23 Armed Group of both Goma International Airport and Kavumu Airport in Bukavu,” Magosi said during the meeting. He said “an urgent diplomatic intervention is needed to open these airports to facilitate delivery of humanitarian assistance and allow SADC and its structures to find an immediate and workable solution for our mission.”

a1484.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a1484.name: Elias Magosi
a1484.title: SADC Executive Secretary
a1484.speech: Noted that such interference — allegations of external support for the M23 rebels — violates international law and defies regional peace agreements.

a1516.speaker: Claver Gatete, UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1516.name: Claver Gatete
a1516.title: UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1516.speech: Said foreign aid is no longer a viable solution for Africa's growing development needs, and that the continent's annual Sustainable Development Goal (SDGs) financing shortfall has reached $1.3 trillion ; "Aid won't close the gap. We must stop exporting raw materials and importing poverty."

a1516.speaker: Claver Gatete, UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1516.name: Claver Gatete
a1516.title: UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1516.speech: Said African leaders need to execute structural reforms to expand domestic resource mobilisation, build regional value chains and shift away from exporting raw commodities; called for greater investment in manufacturing, green industries and youth-led enterprises while noting that more than 80 percent of Africa's exports remain unprocessed.

a1516.speaker: Claver Gatete, UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1516.name: Claver Gatete
a1516.title: UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1516.speech: Reiterated ECA's support for the creation of an African Credit Rating Agency, arguing that current international rating practices distort risk and restrict access to affordable capital; said it is mandatory for African countries to scale blended finance mechanisms, issue local currency bonds and digitize tax and revenue systems to boost efficiency and compliance.

a1516.speaker: UNECA (statement issued on Thursday)
a1516.name: UNECA (statement issued on Thursday)
a1516.speech: Quoted Gatete as saying that the continent's annual Sustainable Development Goal (SDGs) financing shortfall has reached $1.3 trillion.

a1516.speaker: Robinah Nabbanja, Prime Minister of Uganda
a1516.name: Robinah Nabbanja
a1516.title: Prime Minister of Uganda
a1516.speech: Said the continent was "dangerously off track" but highlighted progress made in her country, including reductions in maternal mortality, gains in gender equality and increased national budget allocations linked to the Sustainable Development Goals ; "The Kampala Declaration is practical", adding "We're proud to host this conversation and to take it forward in terms of implementation" ; She said despite this, debt pressures, limited access to concessional finance and the high cost of capital continue to challenge many African economies.

a1536.speaker: John Vorster, South Africa's then Prime Minister
a1536.name: John Vorster
a1536.title: South Africa's then Prime Minister
a1536.speech: Responded to Basil D'Oliveira's inclusion in the England squad by threatening to refuse him entry into the country, saying: "The MCC (England) team is not the team of the MCC but of the anti-apartheid movement."

a1536.speaker: Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC)
a1536.name: Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC)
a1536.speech: Called off the tour because of attempts to influence the selection of the squad.

a1536.speaker: AFP report, later confirmed by New Delhi police
a1536.name: AFP report
a1536.title: later confirmed by New Delhi police
a1536.speech: Said the force had phone recordings of Hansie Cronje and an Indian bookmaker discussing predetermined Proteas' performances during a tour of India in February and March 2000.

a1536.speaker: Hansie Cronje, former South Africa cricket captain
a1536.name: Hansie Cronje
a1536.title: former South Africa cricket captain
a1536.speech: Later confessed to several allegations at the South African government-appointed King Commission, including attempts to bribe team-mates Herschelle Gibbs and Henry Williams to underperform in a one-day international against India; he also admitted to receiving thousands of dollars from bookmakers and gamblers, while insisting he had never thrown a game.

a1536.speaker: Traditionalists (cricket)
a1536.name: Traditionalists (cricket)
a1536.speech: Criticised the contrived nature of the result of the 2000 Centurion Test.

a1837.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1837.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1837.title: President of South Africa
a1837.speech: Said in his annual state of the nation address to Parliament in Cape Town that the country is not prepared to be pushed around by any nation, a statement said to have been made in response to US President Donald Trump: "Right now we are witnessing the rise of nationalism and protectionism" ; "That is the world we are in now, growing the economy is our priority" ; "But let me stress, we will not be bullied, nor will we be derailed. We are resilient, and we will not allow ourselves to be pushed around. We will stand together as a country and speak with one voice in defence of our national interest, our sovereignty and the democracy set out in our Constitution."

a1837.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1837.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1837.title: President of South Africa
a1837.speech: Said in his speech that the country would go through challenges after the suspension of that US funding, while emphasising that they are working to strengthen HIV/AIDS intervention services in the country.

a1837.speaker: Reuters news agency
a1837.name: Reuters news agency
a1837.speech: Reported that Ramaphosa made the remark on Thursday, February 6, 2025, during his annual address to the public, four days after President Trump threatened to cut off all aid provided by the United States to South Africa.

a1837.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States (post on Truth Social)
a1837.name: Donald Trump
a1837.title: President of the United States (post on Truth Social)
a1837.speech: Posted that he would cut off all funding and aid to South Africa over what he claimed: "There is a confiscation of land and certain classes of people are being treated very badly," without naming the people being mistreated by that government ; wrote further that South Africa's leadership has been involved in human rights violations, which he claimed was not being taken seriously by the media in that country ; "South Africa's government is doing strange and unacceptable things," without specifying which things are being done by South Africa.

a1837.speaker: Government of South Africa / Ramaphosa administration
a1837.name: Government of South Africa / Ramaphosa administration
a1837.speech: Has been denying the distortion, saying instead that the expropriation law was aimed at returning unused areas under government administration.

a1837.speaker: Spokesperson of the South African Presidency
a1837.name: Spokesperson of the South African Presidency
a1837.speech: Said Trump's statement was driven by misleading words spread by his aide, the billionaire Elon Musk, who was born in South Africa.

a1837.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire and aide to Trump
a1837.name: Elon Musk
a1837.title: billionaire and aide to Trump
a1837.speech: Has been a major critic of the South African government over what he claims is its oppression of citizens of white origin; has also said the law aims to seize land owned by the minority class (whites) who live in and own a large portion of the land in that country.

a1844.speaker: Tenyson Kaunda, Dedza district tuberculosis officer
a1844.name: Tenyson Kaunda
a1844.title: Dedza district tuberculosis officer
a1844.speech: Disclosed that the district is making remarkable progress in the fight against tuberculosis (TB) and is on track to eliminate it as a public health threat by 2030, and said Dedza has seen a significant improvement in TB treatment outcomes: "Our treatment success rate currently stands at 94 percent, while the death rate has dropped to 4 percent. This is an improvement compared to two years ago, when the treatment success rate was 92 percent and the death rate was 8 percent." ; Noted that the district currently manages about 600 TB patients, including those with multi-drug resistant TB, and that most are responding well to treatment.

a1844.speaker: Tenyson Kaunda, Dedza district tuberculosis officer
a1844.name: Tenyson Kaunda
a1844.title: Dedza district tuberculosis officer
a1844.speech: Attributed the success to the vital role played by community volunteers and the use of mobile screening vans: "Volunteers travel throughout villages to collect sputum samples for early diagnosis, while mobile vans provide screening services in hard-to-reach areas, including border posts where even people coming from Mozambique are screened." ; Added that the vans also visit TB hotspots across the district, contributing to timely identification and treatment of cases.

a1844.speaker: Tenyson Kaunda, Dedza district tuberculosis officer
a1844.name: Tenyson Kaunda
a1844.title: Dedza district tuberculosis officer
a1844.speech: Expressed concern over persistent myths and misconceptions surrounding TB: "In many communities, TB is still associated with HIV, which discourages people from seeking medical help."

a1844.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1844.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1844.speech: Has also set this target - eradicating TB and leprosy by 2030 - globally.

a1844.speaker: Tisungane Mwenyenkulu, Ntlep deputy programme manager
a1844.name: Tisungane Mwenyenkulu
a1844.title: Ntlep deputy programme manager
a1844.speech: Hailed the country's progress in the fight against TB and leprosy: "If we maintain our current momentum, Malawi is well-positioned to eliminate the two diseases by 2030. However, we must continue implementing key interventions and intensify media efforts to keep the public informed."

a1844.speaker: Tamanda Matebule, Malawi Institute of Journalism (MIJ), speaking on behalf of fellow journalists
a1844.name: Tamanda Matebule
a1844.title: Malawi Institute of Journalism (MIJ), speaking on behalf of fellow journalists
a1844.speech: Pledged continued media coverage of TB and leprosy: "We appreciate Ntlep's engagement with the media. These gatherings equip us with knowledge and motivation to do more."

a1844.speaker: National TB and Leprosy Elimination Programme (Ntlep)
a1844.name: National TB and Leprosy Elimination Programme (Ntlep)
a1844.speech: Raised concerns about the recent aid cuts by the US government to the health sector, lamenting that the move will negatively impact efforts to combat TB and leprosy in the country if alternatives or mitigation measures are not devised.

a2055.speaker: Dr Robert Beugré Mambé, Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
a2055.name: Dr Robert Beugré Mambé
a2055.title: Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
a2055.speech: Welcomed the quality and dynamism of the relationship between Côte d'Ivoire and the United States, describing it as a “relationship built on trust, nurtured by rigour and consolidated by concrete results on the projects from which our country benefits” ; “the bilateral compact that is now ending is a perfect illustration of what can be produced by cooperation founded on four things: mutual respect, transparency, responsibility and mutual trust” ; “the results on the ground, beyond the physical infrastructure achievements and the figures, are even more eloquent in terms of the improvement of living conditions and the retreat of poverty.”

a2055.speaker: Dr Robert Beugré Mambé, Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
a2055.name: Dr Robert Beugré Mambé
a2055.title: Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
a2055.speech: Promised that what he described as “the diplomacy of the concrete, which does not only promise but acts and delivers results” would be implemented to make this new partnership an even more resounding success.

a2055.speaker: Alassane Ouattara, President of Côte d'Ivoire (vision cited by the Prime Minister)
a2055.name: Alassane Ouattara
a2055.title: President of Côte d'Ivoire (vision cited by the Prime Minister)
a2055.speech: “Development is not decreed. Development is built with methods, with solid partners and with a constant political will.”

a2055.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a2055.name: Donald Trump
a2055.title: President of the United States
a2055.speech: “America is proud of its friendship with the nations that share its will to build a better world. It aspires, like us, to a future in which every people can prosper in dignity and freedom.”

a2055.speaker: Fidèle Sarassoro, Minister-Director of Cabinet of the President of the Republic and Chairman of the Board of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA Côte d'Ivoire)
a2055.name: Fidèle Sarassoro
a2055.title: Minister-Director of Cabinet of the President of the Republic and Chairman of the Board of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA Côte d'Ivoire)
a2055.speech: Reiterated the commitment of the teams to work towards achieving more significant results: “We are convinced that the experience and the lessons learned from the bilateral compact will allow us in future to avoid the shortcomings observed during its implementation. Likewise, the MCC's eligibility criteria through the Scorecard will continue to guide our efforts to improve our country's performance in matters of governance.”

a2055.speaker: Jason Small, MCC Vice-President for Operations
a2055.name: Jason Small
a2055.title: MCC Vice-President for Operations
a2055.speech: Congratulated Fidèle Sarassoro and the staff of MCA Côte d'Ivoire, welcomed a model that works and the shared belief that economic growth makes itself felt beyond borders, and saluted in particular the numerous road infrastructures, the three technical and vocational training centres, the 40 neighbourhood secondary schools, the two annexes of the École normale supérieure and two campuses built under the bilateral Compact.

a2055.speaker: Jessica Davis Ba, United States Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire
a2055.name: Jessica Davis Ba
a2055.title: United States Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire
a2055.speech: Highlighted the special character of relations between the Ivorian and American governments, pointing out that the regional Compact is the first partnership of this level within the MCC framework that the United States has entered into since President Donald Trump's return to the White House.

a2055.speaker: Christopher Landau, US Deputy Secretary of State (quoted by the Ambassador)
a2055.name: Christopher Landau
a2055.title: US Deputy Secretary of State (quoted by the Ambassador)
a2055.speech: “This pact reflects President Trump's attachment to intelligent and responsible development serving the interests of the United States. A more robust energy sector in West Africa makes it possible to create new markets for American companies, to support employment in the United States and to contribute to regional stability, which is beneficial for all of us.”

a2055.speaker: Mamadou Sangafowa Coulibaly, Minister of Mines, Petroleum and Energy
a2055.name: Mamadou Sangafowa Coulibaly
a2055.title: Minister of Mines, Petroleum and Energy
a2055.speech: Requested further support from the American government in the energy field: “We hope to be able to explore new investment opportunities, notably through an additional Compact aligned with the strategic priorities of our electricity sector”, to cover the “investment needs to modernise our infrastructure, optimise energy distribution and integrate alternative energies” ; undertook to “do everything possible to guarantee a rigorous, transparent and exemplary implementation of this project under the vigilant eye of the head of government.”

a2147.speaker: UK government spokesperson
a2147.name: UK government spokesperson
a2147.speech: Said in a statement that "no further payments in relation to this policy will be made and Rwanda has waived any additional payments." ; said in a statement: "The Home Secretary has been clear that the costly Migration and Economic Development Partnership with Rwanda wasted tax-payer money and should not continue."

a2147.speaker: Yolande Makolo, Rwandan government spokesperson
a2147.name: Yolande Makolo
a2147.title: Rwandan government spokesperson
a2147.speech: Said on Monday that the UK had asked Rwanda to "quietly forgo" the remaining payment - reportedly amounting to 50m pounds ($64m) - based on "trust and good faith" ; said Rwanda would now be "following up" on outstanding payments relating to the migrant deal to which the UK was "legally bound."

a2147.speaker: Yolande Makolo, Rwandan government spokesperson
a2147.name: Yolande Makolo
a2147.title: Rwandan government spokesperson
a2147.speech: Said on Monday that the aid cuts amounted to "unjustified punitive measures to coerce Rwanda into compromising our national security."

a2147.speaker: Rwandan government
a2147.name: Rwandan government
a2147.speech: Has asked the UK to pay the remainder of the money it says it is owed, accusing the UK of breaching trust by suspending some aid to the country; Rwanda has often denied backing the M23 rebel group, but has recently been more defensive, saying it has had to take measures to deal with the "existential threat" posed by genocidal militia near its borders.

a2147.speaker: UK government
a2147.name: UK government
a2147.speech: Announced it would halt bilateral aid to Rwanda last month, except for "support to the poorest and most vulnerable", after accusing the country of supporting M23, a rebel group that has captured swathes of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

a2147.speaker: UN experts
a2147.name: UN experts
a2147.speech: Have previously estimated that between 3,000 and 4,000 Rwandan troops are in eastern DR Congo.

a2147.speaker: Sir Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister
a2147.name: Sir Keir Starmer
a2147.title: UK Prime Minister
a2147.speech: Speaking in July last year, shortly after being elected, said the plan was "dead and buried", arguing that the scheme had "never been a deterrent" and would only deport "less than 1%" of small boat arrivals.

a2198.speaker: Paulo Duarte, new coach of the Syli National (Guinea national football team) — "Projet sportif Guinée 2030" document
a2198.name: Paulo Duarte
a2198.title: new coach of the Syli National (Guinea national football team) — "Projet sportif Guinée 2030" document
a2198.speech: A 23-page document setting out short-, medium- and long-term objectives, including supporting the organisation of the National Technical Directorate (DTN), accompanying the DTN's areas of intervention, developing grassroots football, strengthening coaches' technical skills, developing local championships, promoting women's football, contributing to the fulfilment of athletes' potential, encouraging the export of talent to Europe, and encouraging the development of local clubs.

a2198.speaker: Paulo Duarte, new coach of the Syli National — "Projet sportif Guinée 2030" document (short-term objectives)
a2198.name: Paulo Duarte
a2198.title: new coach of the Syli National — "Projet sportif Guinée 2030" document (short-term objectives)
a2198.speech: According to the document, in the short term the main objective will be borne directly by the coach, who will take on the mission of implementing a new style of play for the National Team of the Republic of Guinea, reflecting a clear collective identity founded on principles of organisation, positive aggressiveness, verticality and tactical intelligence, while respecting the athletic and technical profile of the Guinean player; the coach will lead a rigorous process of analysing the team's strengths and weaknesses, and will promote a strong, transformative mindset centred on professionalism, responsibility, dedication and collective work — it will not only be about preparing matches, but about forming men, transforming the group into a symbol of national identity.

a2198.speaker: Paulo Duarte, new coach of the Syli National — "Projet sportif Guinée 2030" document (medium- and long-term objectives)
a2198.name: Paulo Duarte
a2198.title: new coach of the Syli National — "Projet sportif Guinée 2030" document (medium- and long-term objectives)
a2198.speech: In the medium term, the priority will be preparation for the qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (CAN), an objective which is not limited to participation but aims to affirm the Republic of Guinea as a strong nation in African football; the major long-term objective is qualification for the 2030 World Cup, requiring a strategic vision, continuity of the work undertaken, and structural investment at all levels, with the coach as the architect of development.

a2324.speaker: U.N. World Food Programme (WFP)
a2324.name: U.N. World Food Programme (WFP)
a2324.speech: Said the United States has lifted a pause on food donations: "We can confirm that the recent pause concerning in-kind food assistance to WFP - purchased from U.S. farmers with Title II funds - has been rescinded. This allows for the resumption of food purchases and deliveries under existing USAID agreements," WFP said in an X post on Sunday.

a2324.speaker: U.S. State Department
a2324.name: U.S. State Department
a2324.speech: Did not respond to a request for comment.

a2324.speaker: Humanitarian officials
a2324.name: Humanitarian officials
a2324.speech: Say a lack of detail in the Trump administration's effort to slash and reshape U.S. foreign aid has created chaos and confusion, leaving them to work out whether to take the financial risk of continuing programs without assurance that they are covered by a waiver.

a2324.speaker: Office of Inspector General for USAID (report released Monday)
a2324.name: Office of Inspector General for USAID (report released Monday)
a2324.speech: Said that "uncertainty put more than $489 million of food assistance at ports, in transit, and in warehouses at risk of spoilage, unanticipated storage needs, and diversion"; the auditor's report said USAID staff had identified more than 500,000 metric tons of food currently at sea or ready to be shipped that had been sourced under the Title II program, and that "Because this funding source was not included under the Secretary's emergency food assistance waiver, these commodities were held in limbo, subjecting them to spoilage, unanticipated storage needs, and potential diversion."

a2415.speaker: UN State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) report
a2415.name: UN State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) report
a2415.speech: New UN report shows 733 million people are food insecure; the report's theme, "Financing to End Hunger, Food Insecurity and Malnutrition in All its Forms," highlights the dramatically inadequate funding provided by the international community for hunger assistance, noting food security and nutrition represent less than a quarter of the total funding for official development assistance and that the financing gap could amount to several trillion GBP; it also reports that throughout 2022 the average cost of a healthy diet rose globally to 3.96 PPP dollars per person per day compared to 3.56 PPP in 2021, and that hunger is increasing in Africa at an alarming rate, where one in every 5 people is hungry.

a2415.speaker: Kate Munro, Head of Advocacy at Action Against Hunger UK
a2415.name: Kate Munro
a2415.title: Head of Advocacy at Action Against Hunger UK
a2415.speech: "Conflict, climate change, and chronic inequality are major drivers behind surging food insecurity. The good news is that the international community has the tools and the knowledge to prevent hunger for everyone, for good. Yet, unless we close the growing gap between community needs and available funding, this preventable crisis will continue." ; "Financing for hunger assistance programs shouldn't be considered a cost, but an investment in the long-term security of our global community. The SOFI report makes clear that our current food system is unsustainable. We need a rapid and sustained influx of funding for multidimensional programs that address the nexus between hunger, climate, conflict and gender. The world's most vulnerable are counting on us."

a2415.speaker: Action Against Hunger's 2024 Hunger Funding Gap report
a2415.name: Action Against Hunger's 2024 Hunger Funding Gap report
a2415.speech: Highlighted the gap in hunger funding for countries with the most urgent needs, up 23 per cent from 2022 to 2023.

a2658.speaker: Jackline Nasiwa, South Sudanese activist
a2658.name: Jackline Nasiwa
a2658.title: South Sudanese activist
a2658.speech: Has urged South Sudan's leadership to immediately audit all revenue collections and implement transparent financial practices, as the nation's economic crisis deepens and international aid significantly shrinks. Speaking to Eye Radio on Thursday, July 3, she underscored the urgent need for robust accountability, particularly in light of a projected humanitarian crisis. Highlighted South Sudan's unique challenges, including its reliance on oil revenues now impacted by the Sudanese conflict, which leaves “a huge gap in terms of the revenues generated.” “This is a lesson for the government to put up proper accountability and transparent processes for the utilization and usage of this money,” Jackline stated. She pointed out that the government need to properly manage all revenue streams, not just oil, adding that South Sudanese citizens must see their taxes translated into tangible services. “We pay taxes monthly to the government, and we want to see that the taxes that we pay are reflected in the services that we get,” she said. With international funding cuts becoming a “global” trend, Nasiwa stressed that the onus is now on the government to meticulously manage its resources. “Where there is a gap left, the government has to come in handy and implement strict measures in terms of the exploration of our resources and also their utilization.”

a2658.speaker: Studies in The Lancet
a2658.name: Studies in The Lancet
a2658.speech: Warn that over 14 million people globally, many of them children, could die prematurely by 2030 due to severe cuts in U.S. foreign aid initiated by the Trump administration.

a2658.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a2658.name: Marco Rubio
a2658.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a2658.speech: Confirmed in March that over 80% of USAID programs have been cancelled.

a2746.speaker: MCC executive (anonymous, at staff meeting)
a2746.name: MCC executive (anonymous
a2746.title: at staff meeting)
a2746.speech: Told staff that “we are coming to an orderly close” with all programs to be discontinued, according to an employee who was present.

a2746.speaker: MCC staff-wide memo (seen by AFP)
a2746.name: MCC staff-wide memo (seen by AFP)
a2746.speech: Informed that billionaire Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency was imposing a “significant reduction” at MCC and laid out practicalities for the majority of staff who will lose jobs.

a2746.speaker: MCC employee (anonymous, speaking on condition of anonymity to avoid retribution)
a2746.name: MCC employee (anonymous
a2746.title: speaking on condition of anonymity to avoid retribution)
a2746.speech: Said the organization differed significantly from USAID: “We're not doing humanitarian assistance. We're not doing social justice. We're very much building up an environment for private-sector investment in foreign economies” ; “This is a very different thing, something that actually does put America first” ; “It's interesting, if we're worried about China's influence in the world, that we would shutter MCC, which builds large-scale infrastructure that counters China's influence.” ; Said MCC will inform countries on Friday that compacts will be terminated within 40 days, and that after negotiations with Musk's team MCC was allowed extensions in four countries; the goal is “so someone is not going to fall into a pit or something” — “Whether or not we'll be successful, I don't know.”

a2746.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, Zambian President
a2746.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a2746.title: Zambian President
a2746.speech: Vowed in October to keep upholding “shared values” with the United States as he signed a half-billion-dollar agreement to improve roads, irrigation and electricity.

a2746.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
a2746.name: Xi Jinping
a2746.title: Chinese President
a2746.speech: Vowed in September another $51 billion of investment in Africa over the next three years.

a2746.speaker: Elizabeth Hoffman, executive director for North America at ONE
a2746.name: Elizabeth Hoffman
a2746.title: executive director for North America at ONE
a2746.speech: Voiced alarm at the shutdown: “MCC brings an innovative and entrepreneurial approach to development assistance that holds governments accountable and effectively counters malign foreign influences like China,” she said.

a2746.speaker: MCC and Trump administration (non-response)
a2746.name: MCC and Trump administration (non-response)
a2746.speech: Did not immediately comment on the cuts, which were first reported by development specialist site Devex.

a2819.speaker: Memo signed by Gabriel Aduda, Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Defence
a2819.name: Memo signed by Gabriel Aduda
a2819.title: Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Defence
a2819.speech: According to the memo, Shamseldeen Babatunde Ogunjimi was reported to have come fourth in the examination for the selection of the Accountant General, scoring 62 per cent in the written examination.

a2819.speaker: Mojisola Meranda / Mudashiru Obasa, Lagos State House of Assembly (Obasa, former/restored Speaker)
a2819.name: Mojisola Meranda / Mudashiru Obasa
a2819.title: Lagos State House of Assembly (Obasa, former/restored Speaker)
a2819.speech: Obasa demanded that the legislators should come and pay homage to him, but only four of them turned up.

a2819.speaker: Supreme Court of Nigeria (ruling)
a2819.name: Supreme Court of Nigeria (ruling)
a2819.speech: Threw out the elections Governor Fubara organised into the Rivers State local government councils; recognised as legitimate the legislators who had sworn to impeach him after he challenged their right to abandon the party on whose tickets they won elections to join the ruling party; and instructed the Central Bank to stop sending monies to the State Government.

a2819.speaker: A senator, speaking on Channels Television (unnamed)
a2819.name: A senator
a2819.title: speaking on Channels Television (unnamed)
a2819.speech: Complained bitterly that he saw his colleague, Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, come into the Chambers with her husband and he kissed her; it was totally unacceptable for a husband to kiss his wife in the Chambers, he explained.

a2819.speaker: Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, Nigerian Senator
a2819.name: Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan
a2819.title: Nigerian Senator
a2819.speech: Had made disturbing allegations of sexual harassment against the President of the Senate.

a2819.speaker: Mr Imasuen, Senate Committee Chairman
a2819.name: Mr Imasuen
a2819.title: Senate Committee Chairman
a2819.speech: The argument used by the Committee Chairman was that “Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan's petition violated the Senate's procedural rules, as she had personally signed the document.”

a2819.speaker: Confidential report obtained by Nairametrics from a source tracking motor tanker vessels (Motor Tanker Vessels report)
a2819.name: Confidential report obtained by Nairametrics from a source tracking motor tanker vessels (Motor Tanker Vessels report)
a2819.speech: Revealed that the Nigeria National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) imported 159,000 metric tons of Premium Motor Spirit between 1 February and 12 February, translating to approximately 213 million litres of petrol.

a2819.speaker: Nigeria National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL)
a2819.name: Nigeria National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL)
a2819.speech: In December 2024, announced the restart of the 125,000 barrels per day Warri Refinery and Petrochemical Company (WRPC), which was approved for rehabilitation in 2021 for $897 million.

a2819.speaker: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a2819.name: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a2819.speech: Set a January deadline for the adoption of cleaner fuels and vehicles to reduce air pollution across the region.

a2917.speaker: UNRWA (update on the situation in Gaza)
a2917.name: UNRWA (update on the situation in Gaza)
a2917.speech: Lamented that humanitarian conditions continue to be “catastrophic” despite the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas that came into force on Sunday, 19 January, and said Gaza is “the most dangerous place for humanitarian workers” ; stated that the ceasefire is “only a starting point” for responding to the needs of the inhabitants of Gaza, who are “devastated” after more than 15 months of “violence, displacement and siege” ; reported that despite “all the obstacles” hundreds of UNRWA trucks carrying humanitarian aid have entered Gaza since the beginning of the ceasefire, that the equivalent of about 7,000 trucks are ready to be delivered and another 1,521 are in the process of being procured ; and warned that at least 1.9 million people (about 90% of the population) were displaced during the war, many of them more than ten times.

a2917.speaker: Palestinian Ministry of Health (data collected by UNRWA)
a2917.name: Palestinian Ministry of Health (data collected by UNRWA)
a2917.speech: According to its data, at least 47,161 people have been killed and 111,166 wounded since 7 October 2023; of the dead, 13,319 were children and 786 were less than one year old.

a2917.speaker: Philippe Lazzarini, UNRWA Commissioner-General
a2917.name: Philippe Lazzarini
a2917.title: UNRWA Commissioner-General
a2917.speech: Explained that many of the displaced are trying to return to their homes, most of which have disappeared, with more than 90% of homes estimated damaged or destroyed and rubble amounting to more than 50 million tonnes; and warned of the “immense health challenges ahead”, since almost all of Gaza’s hospitals are damaged or partially destroyed, while some 30,000 people are suffering life-changing injuries requiring continuous rehabilitation.

a2917.speaker: António Costa, President of the European Council (post on the social network X)
a2917.name: António Costa
a2917.title: President of the European Council (post on the social network X)
a2917.speech: Said on Thursday that he hoped for support in the face of “enormous humanitarian needs” in Gaza during the ceasefire: “It was good to meet today with Philippe Lazzarini. UNRWA is playing a crucial role in supporting the civilian population in Gaza, the West Bank and across the region” ; recalled that “during the implementation phase of the ceasefire, humanitarian needs will be enormous” in the Gaza Strip.

a2917.speaker: Israel
a2917.name: Israel
a2917.speech: Accused nine UNRWA staff members — out of a total of 14,000 — of having been involved in the 7 October attack; they were subsequently dismissed.

a2940.speaker: Moussa Diallo, head of Component 3 of the "Sariya Bato" programme
a2940.name: Moussa Diallo
a2940.title: head of Component 3 of the "Sariya Bato" programme
a2940.speech: Said the session was organised in collaboration with the Coalition of Civil Society Organisations for the Fight against Corruption and Poverty (COSCLCCP), the Malian Network of Investigative Journalists (RMJI) and the management of the Higher School of Journalism and Communication Sciences (ESJSC).

a2940.speaker: Jean La Voix, "Sariya Bato"
a2940.name: Jean La Voix
a2940.title: "Sariya Bato"
a2940.speech: Stressed that, unlike the "Mali Justice Project", "Sariya Bato" has broadened its field of action; said the work of the actors gathered during this training is very important in the fight against corruption; insisted on certain aspects of this fight such as the concern for truth, discretion, confidentiality, the safety of journalists and rigour in the work so as not to sully citizens' reputations; invited the various actors to work as a network in order to obtain more results.

a2940.speaker: Ibrahima Sylla, facilitator of the session
a2940.name: Ibrahima Sylla
a2940.title: facilitator of the session
a2940.speech: Gave several presentations, notably on "the national anti-corruption strategy adopted by the government of Mali", "the factors favouring corruption in Mali", "the main causes of corruption", "the links in the anti-corruption chain: the actors and their missions" and "the common forms of corruption"; insisted on the highly sensitive nature of information related to corruption.

a2940.speaker: Aboubacar Warma, student at the Higher School of Journalism and Communication Sciences (ESJSC)
a2940.name: Aboubacar Warma
a2940.title: student at the Higher School of Journalism and Communication Sciences (ESJSC)
a2940.speech: "Over these two days, we were informed about the mechanisms of corruption and we received techniques for investigating and denouncing actions linked to corruption, while avoiding as far as possible exposing ourselves to potential dangers. We were also invited to play an active role in implementing the 'anti-corruption strategy', whose Axis 4 is devoted to communication, hence the need to involve media and communication professionals."

a2940.speaker: Ahmed Sekou Diallo, President of the Coalition of Civil Society Organisations for the Fight against Corruption and Poverty (COSCLCCP)
a2940.name: Ahmed Sekou Diallo
a2940.title: President of the Coalition of Civil Society Organisations for the Fight against Corruption and Poverty (COSCLCCP)
a2940.speech: Wished to thank the head of Component 3 of "Sariya Bato"; also thanked the participants for their quality contributions.

a2940.speaker: Dr Tounkara of the ESJSC, on behalf of the participants
a2940.name: Dr Tounkara of the ESJSC
a2940.title: on behalf of the participants
a2940.speech: Thanked the Sariya Bato Project for this welcome initiative. "This training was an opportunity. We were informed but we were not trained. We want other initiatives to follow in the interest of the beneficiaries," he stressed.

a2940.speaker: Moussa Diallo, head of Component 3 of the "Sariya Bato" programme
a2940.name: Moussa Diallo
a2940.title: head of Component 3 of the "Sariya Bato" programme
a2940.speech: Stressed at the end of the training that one of the objectives had been achieved by bringing together CSOs, the media and academics in a common dynamic against the scourge; said this training is the beginning of a process that will connect the actors concerned by Strategic Axis 4 of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy.

a2952.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Djibouti's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a2952.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a2952.title: Djibouti's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a2952.speech: Took the opportunity to call on the United States to redouble its efforts to support Djibouti's initiatives aimed at promoting sustainable economic and social development; expressed the need for a strengthened partnership to respond to the regional threats weighing on security and prosperity.

a3199.speaker: Wale Edun, Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3199.name: Wale Edun
a3199.title: Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3199.speech: Announced on Saturday in Washington, on the sidelines of the spring meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, that the United States has expressed its willingness to invest in the strategic Nigeria-Morocco Gas Pipeline (NMGP) project, and said the discussions held with American officials highlighted Washington's interest in supporting the structural reforms under way in Nigeria with a view to strengthening the confidence of international investors ; “One of the main points of attention concerns American investments in the Nigerian natural gas sector, in particular the Nigeria-Morocco gas pipeline project, given the country's substantial reserves,” he specified, as quoted by the Nigerian outlet The Cable.

a3199.speaker: Wale Edun, Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3199.name: Wale Edun
a3199.title: Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3199.speech: Indicated that several projects led by American companies could contribute to the development of Nigeria's digital connectivity.

a3199.speaker: Wale Edun, Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3199.name: Wale Edun
a3199.title: Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3199.speech: Stressed that the United States has expressed its willingness to help Nigeria cope with the financing difficulties caused by the drawdown of USAID activities, by offering increased technical assistance.

a3199.speaker: Washington (US officials)
a3199.name: Washington (US officials)
a3199.speech: Made known its intention to support initiatives designed to improve productivity, strengthen value chains and ensure food security through targeted investments and reinforced technical support.

a3199.speaker: The Cable (Nigerian media outlet)
a3199.name: The Cable (Nigerian media outlet)
a3199.speech: Cited as the source quoting Wale Edun's remarks on American investment in the Nigerian gas sector.

a3297.speaker: Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a3297.name: Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a3297.speech: Said the decline in official development assistance is because globally, almost all countries, including those which provide development assistance to countries such as Malawi, are facing macroeconomic challenges.

a3297.speaker: Bertha Bangara Chikadza, Ecama acting president
a3297.name: Bertha Bangara Chikadza
a3297.title: Ecama acting president
a3297.speech: In a written response, observed that the dwindling ODA has a number of implications on Malawi, because grants have played a vital role in addressing Malawi's socio-economic challenges such as health, education, and infrastructure: "This means a decrease in ODA grants impact the delivery of essential services and hinder poverty reduction efforts. Although concessional loans have favourable terms [lower interest rates, longer repayment periods] compared to commercial loans, they still need to be repaid." ; "Therefore, with the current debt sustainability problem, the country must manage its debt burden carefully. Thus rising concessional loans could add to the existing strain on the country's debt-to-gross domestic product [GDP] ratio."

a3297.speaker: Bertha Bangara Chikadza, Ecama acting president
a3297.name: Bertha Bangara Chikadza
a3297.title: Ecama acting president
a3297.speech: Observed that although it is important that the country strikes a balance between grants and loans, long term solutions should be sought: "We should continue to explore alternative funding sources such as private investment or domestic revenue mobilisation which are sustainable." ; "This just shows that we cannot rely on aid forever and there is need for serious policy reforms, especially in governance, improving tax collection, and enhancing public financial management."

a3297.speaker: Bertha Bangara Chikadza, Ecama acting president
a3297.name: Bertha Bangara Chikadza
a3297.title: Ecama acting president
a3297.speech: Urged authorities to "closely monitor the shift" from grants to loans, ensuring prudent debt management and maximising development impact: "A strategic approach is necessary to navigate this transition effectively."

a3297.speaker: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (Unctad) data
a3297.name: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (Unctad) data
