a3297.speech: Showing that aid inflows to LDCs such as Malawi declined by four percent in 2022, falling to $62 billion (K109 trillion), following an eight percent decrease the previous year, and that LDCs' share of global ODA decreased to 22 percent in 2022, the lowest in over a decade ; over the past decade, the share of loans in total ODA more than doubled for Latin America and the Caribbean, to 49 percent in 2022, increased to 40 percent for Asia and Oceania and to 29 percent for Africa.

a3297.speaker: UN
a3297.name: UN
a3297.speech: Said that aid is also being increasingly provided through concessional loans rather than grants, increasing developing countries' debt burdens at a time of growing debt distress.

a3297.speaker: Christopher Mbukwa, Mzuzu University economics lecturer
a3297.name: Christopher Mbukwa
a3297.title: Mzuzu University economics lecturer
a3297.speech: Observes that Malawi has economically struggled in spite of steady flow of ODA and low interest loans for years, though these have helped to stabilise some short-term economic imbalances such as bridging the forex shortages: "We may not worry much because these have had little effect in catalysing our economic growth. On the other hand, these have been essential in improving our import cover." ; "We have economically struggled as a country in spite of growing inflows of ODA. So perhaps, it is high time we started to concentrate on raising our domestic revenue generation efforts." ; said Malawi Revenue Authority's ability to beat its targets in two years running speaks of our capacity to raise more.

a3297.speaker: Betchani Tchereni, Treasury Secretary
a3297.name: Betchani Tchereni
a3297.title: Treasury Secretary
a3297.speech: Concedes that following Covid-19 and other global exogenous factors, aid has been falling: "But the steps taken by Malawi through the budget, for example, are in the right direction where 30 percent of the budget looks at production." ; "It is because we realise that the future is not in aid, it is in diversifying the economy."

a3297.speaker: World Bank data
a3297.name: World Bank data
a3297.speech: Showing Malawi's debt service payments, which include principal and interest, has risen from $54 million (about K95 billion) in 2018 to $101 million (K175 billion) in 2022.

a3370.speaker: Ministry of Health Second Quarter Performance Report (Eswatini)
a3370.name: Ministry of Health Second Quarter Performance Report (Eswatini)
a3370.speech: Shows that between March and September 2025 a total of 216 retail pharmacies were inspected following the national registration call, of which only 45 were compliant while 171 were non-compliant due to a lack of registration, the absence of qualified pharmacists, unsuitable premises or failure to follow good pharmacy practices ; states that post-market surveillance revealed even greater risks, with inspections uncovering pharmacies dispensing expired and recalled drugs and in some cases deliberately altering expiry dates: “These violations undermine safety protocols and expose the public to ineffective or harmful medicines, highlighting the urgent need for stronger regulatory enforcement and monitoring.”

a3370.speaker: Ministry of Health Second Quarter Performance Report (Eswatini)
a3370.name: Ministry of Health Second Quarter Performance Report (Eswatini)
a3370.speech: States that during the review period all cold chain products received at the Central Medical Stores (CMS) were of good quality, with no temperature excursions reported, reflecting progress in safeguarding product integrity ; notes that the substandard condition of CMS transport vehicles poses a serious risk to temperature-sensitive medicines, and that this concern has been formally raised with management.

a3370.speaker: Ministry of Health of Eswatini
a3370.name: Ministry of Health of Eswatini
a3370.speech: Highlighted in the report that non-compliant pharmacies are required to address these gaps through Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) ; said that to strengthen reporting practices the Pharmacovigilance Unit is planning to conduct on-site sensitisation training sessions across health facilities, and stated that one training session was successfully conducted at the Manzini Government Hospital.

a3370.speaker: Ministry of Health Second Quarter Performance Report (Eswatini)
a3370.name: Ministry of Health Second Quarter Performance Report (Eswatini)
a3370.speech: Mentioned that activities implemented by the Medicines Regulatory Unit continue to strengthen the national medical products regulatory system in Eswatini, and highlighted that as the Ministry of Health enhances medical product availability through the transformation of the Central Medical Stores into a semi-autonomous entity, the MRU’s stewardship role in ensuring product safety, efficacy and quality becomes increasingly vital.

a3370.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister for Health of Eswatini
a3370.name: Mduduzi Matsebula
a3370.title: Minister for Health of Eswatini
a3370.speech: Said in his preamble presented to the portfolio committee that the ministry situates health as a driver of Eswatini’s development, closely linking Universal Health Coverage (UHC) with economic growth and productivity ; said the Q2 2025/26 achievements demonstrate resilience despite global funding disruptions and external donor policy shocks ; said internationally, many low- and middle-income countries are grappling with similar challenges—balancing donor dependency with domestic financing, scaling digital health and sustaining momentum on the Sustainable Development Goals amid fiscal pressures.

a3370.speaker: Ministry of Health of Eswatini (second quarter performance report)
a3370.name: Ministry of Health of Eswatini (second quarter performance report)
a3370.speech: Said that out of 480 targeted vacancies only 92 have been filled, which reflects the severe workforce gap that places Eswatini below the WHO-recommended health worker density: “These shortages mirror regional challenges of attrition and migration, but they also create opportunities to strengthen domestic financing, adopt task-shifting models and re-engage the diaspora for specialised support” ; highlighted that with its robust policy base and ongoing recruitment and training reforms, Eswatini can turn its challenges into a platform for innovation and sustainability toward achieving universal health coverage ; said delayed recruitment approvals, unreported exits and the loss of partner-funded positions threaten service continuity.

a3370.speaker: Ministry of Health of Eswatini (second quarter performance report)
a3370.name: Ministry of Health of Eswatini (second quarter performance report)
a3370.speech: States that some officers are employed by partners who indicated that they would not be renewing contracts after September 30, 2025, with affected departments including the Laboratory, HIV/AIDS Programme, Strategic Information and Central Medical Stores ; said that in collaboration with a supporting partner it is conducting an impact assessment regarding human resources for health that were funded by partners ; states that to renew contracts for 260 officers who were previously supported by USAID, a new partner—RISE—has committed to provide support.

a3418.speaker: Malawi (government appeal)
a3418.name: Malawi (government appeal)
a3418.speech: Is appealing to rich nations to walk the talk on previous climate change commitments made during COP 28 in Dubai, as the world converges on Baku, Azerbaijan for COP 29.

a3418.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice President of Malawi
a3418.name: Michael Usi
a3418.title: Vice President of Malawi
a3418.speech: Urged Edinburgh, during a bilateral meeting with Scotland's Acting Cabinet Secretary for Net Zero and Energy, to advocate for developed countries to fulfil their COP28 commitments to the Loss and Damage Fund aimed at addressing irreversible climate impacts.

a3418.speaker: Gillian Martin, Scotland's Acting Cabinet Secretary for Net Zero and Energy
a3418.name: Gillian Martin
a3418.title: Scotland's Acting Cabinet Secretary for Net Zero and Energy
a3418.speech: Highlighted Scotland's leadership as the first global north nation to pledge 10 million pounds specifically for loss and damage.

a3444.speaker: Denis Mukwege, Nobel Peace Prize laureate
a3444.name: Denis Mukwege
a3444.title: Nobel Peace Prize laureate
a3444.speech: Issued a forceful reminder when he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize: African countries are among the richest on the planet, but their people are among the poorest in the world.

a3444.speaker: World Bank (2018 Doing Business rankings)
a3444.name: World Bank (2018 Doing Business rankings)
a3444.speech: Ranked Djibouti as having leapt 55 places in one year and as one of the top 10 most improved economies for ease of doing business.

a3444.speaker: African Development Bank (new forecasts)
a3444.name: African Development Bank (new forecasts)
a3444.speech: Suggest that the continent's infrastructure needs equate to approximately $150bn a year, with a funding deficit in the region of $68bn to $108bn.

a3478.speaker: Avelino Bonifacio, President of the Cape Verdean Swimming Federation
a3478.name: Avelino Bonifacio
a3478.title: President of the Cape Verdean Swimming Federation
a3478.speech: Assured that Cape Verde will take "the largest and most representative delegation ever", since the country is banking on a fusion between the diaspora community and resident athletes ; "With these athletes we will be able to take part in almost all the events in the competition, including the relays, both men's and women's as well as mixed."

a3726.speaker: Shanel Ngowi, Managing Director of S and J Animal Tech Company Limited
a3726.name: Shanel Ngowi
a3726.title: Managing Director of S and J Animal Tech Company Limited
a3726.speech: Says electronic ear tagging of cattle in Tanzania is part of a broader effort to enhance livestock identification, registration and traceability, aiming to improve disease control, enhance food safety and boost market access ; “This system, known as TANLITS (a web-based system developed to operationalise the Livestock Identification, Registration and Traceability), utilises electronic ear tags to track individual animals, allowing for efficient monitoring of vaccinations, disease outbreaks and livestock movements” ; noted that the government has been working to implement this system nationwide, but it has faced some challenges, including low registration rates and suspension of the exercise for assessment ; said that electronic ear tags contain a unique RFID microchip that allows for automatic identification and recording of animal information, enabling tracking of animals from farm to market and across borders; said EID tags help farmers keep accurate records and manage their herds more effectively; said the goal is to establish a robust national livestock identification system using electronic ear tags to enhance the overall livestock sector ; “Enhanced record keeping is another one, whereby data like birth date, sex, parentage, weight and health history can be linked to the unique tag ID, streamlining farm management. Efficient management: EID systems allow for automated data collection and analysis, leading to more efficient management practices and potentially increased productivity” ; said in an exclusive interview in Dar es Salaam that this move will not only modernise the sector, but would also place the country in the global meat market: “We want to bring the value of red meat to the world market by implementing this system that will revamp, restructure and foster the livestock sector to have international standards” ; added that they were eyeing to sell more quality red meat in the export market if stakeholders in the country would support government efforts in implementing effectively a two-strategy system, and said the new method of identification of livestock would strengthen the availability of statistics, put an end to cattle theft and introduce the country to the world meat market.

a3726.speaker: Angello Mwilawa, Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries Director of Research, Training and Extension
a3726.name: Angello Mwilawa
a3726.title: Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries Director of Research, Training and Extension
a3726.speech: Said the ministry had set up various research and training centres to groom young graduates to adopt the system of a feedlot that goes hand in hand with government’s efforts in introducing TANLITS ; “The government wants to revolutionise this livestock sector to become more competitive and attract more young graduates to utilise existing opportunities in the global market because there is demand for red meat” ; explained that the ministry had so far eight training and research centres of incubators – three in Tanga, three in Mwanza, Misungwi and two in Karagwe – and had a total of 240 young graduates from Livestock Training Agents and Sokoine University of Agriculture (SUA); stressed that the livestock feedlot system was going to be a game changer for the growth of the sector in terms of GDP ; “In fact, the government has financed these young graduates to develop their skills by feeding cattle and looking for the market in fish processing industries in the country. This programme will eventually shine in the global market if stakeholders in the sector agree to utilise TANLITS.”

a4208.speaker: Ukrainian authorities
a4208.name: Ukrainian authorities
a4208.speech: Reported that the new night-time Russian attacks on Kyiv killed one person and injured at least six.

a4208.speaker: Local authorities (Kyiv)
a4208.name: Local authorities (Kyiv)
a4208.speech: Said the large-scale drone and missile attack caused several fires throughout the city, including in residential buildings, a daycare centre, open-air kiosks and a metro station.

a4208.speaker: Tymur Tkachenko, head of the military administration of the city of Kyiv
a4208.name: Tymur Tkachenko
a4208.title: head of the military administration of the city of Kyiv
a4208.speech: Declared that the entrance to the Lukianivska metro station was damaged, but that there were no casualties recorded.

a4208.speaker: Vitali Klitschko, Mayor of Kyiv
a4208.name: Vitali Klitschko
a4208.title: Mayor of Kyiv
a4208.speech: Announced that the daycare centre caught fire following the attack.

a4488.speaker: Government Communications Service (Ethiopia)
a4488.name: Government Communications Service (Ethiopia)
a4488.speech: According to the Government Communications Service, over 1.76 million people have been displaced in the Amhara and Afar regional states as a result of the ongoing armed conflict, with the figure standing at over one million people in the Amhara region alone ; According to the Service, over 300,000qtl of food aid was delivered to the internally displaced persons (IDPs) in the two regional states last week.

a4488.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a4488.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a4488.speech: Said last week that the number of people requiring food aid in war-torn northern Ethiopia had surged to more than nine million.

a4501.speaker: Ibrahim Rachid, administrative manager at the Port of Djibouti
a4501.name: Ibrahim Rachid
a4501.title: administrative manager at the Port of Djibouti
a4501.speech: "In the coming decades, the public authorities intend to develop port infrastructure and fishing activities, as well as boating and merchant fleets, in order to set up an accelerator of initiatives in favour of a new generation of sea entrepreneurs."

a4565.speaker: Anita Kiki Gbeho, officer-in-charge of the UN Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNSOM)
a4565.name: Anita Kiki Gbeho
a4565.title: officer-in-charge of the UN Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNSOM)
a4565.speech: Said the Al-Shabaab militant group continues to pose a serious threat to peace and security in Somalia ; told the UN Security Council in a briefing that 2022 was the deadliest year for civilians in the country since 2017, with a 60 percent increase in civilian casualties compared with 2021 ; said the Somali federal government has made progress in countering the threat by targeting Al-Shabaab's military and financial operations and ideological narrative, and that Somali security forces reinforced by local militias have conducted successful operations in Hirshabelle and Galmudug states, with operations expected to gradually move into other areas ; “Consolidating gains in the newly recovered areas will require strong linkages between military operations and stabilization initiatives, comprised of reconciliation and justice components and aimed at bolstering good governance and service delivery” ; said the government continues efforts toward generating forces to gradually assume security responsibilities in line with the Somali transition plan, but that funding for the security transition remains a critical challenge.

a4565.speaker: Anita Kiki Gbeho, officer-in-charge of the UN Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNSOM)
a4565.name: Anita Kiki Gbeho
a4565.title: officer-in-charge of the UN Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNSOM)
a4565.speech: Said that with five consecutive poor rainy seasons the current drought is unprecedented in Somalia and humanitarian needs continue to steadily rise, with about 8.3 million people, nearly half of Somalia's estimated population, requiring assistance and protection in 2023 ; said that thanks to generous donor support, government efforts and local community initiatives, humanitarian organizations scaled up response and reached 7.3 million people in 2022 ; warned that while famine has been prevented for now, it remains a threat if the April-June rains underperform as forecast and humanitarian assistance is not sustained ; called on donors to stand with Somalia by responding to the newly launched 2023 humanitarian response plan seeking 2.6 billion U.S. dollars to meet the priority needs of 7.6 million Somalis ; said the United Nations stands ready to support Somalia in implementing its vision of a secure, stable, and peaceful nation.

a4568.speaker: Dr Olusegun Ogboye, Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health
a4568.name: Dr Olusegun Ogboye
a4568.title: Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health
a4568.speech: Emphasised the importance of the survey in strengthening evidence-based planning for the HIV response: “This is an impact survey that will assess HIV prevalence, treatment coverage, and viral load suppression among adults in Lagos. We count on the cooperation of communities, security agencies, and field workers to make it successful” ; urged field workers to approach their tasks with diligence: “Even though you are one individual in one community, the results you generate will shape national health planning. The success of this survey depends on every one of us.”

a4568.speaker: Dr Ibrahim Dalhatu, Deputy Director of Epidemiology and Strategic Information, U.S. CDC
a4568.name: Dr Ibrahim Dalhatu
a4568.title: Deputy Director of Epidemiology and Strategic Information, U.S. CDC
a4568.speech: Described the initiative as a people-centred activity despite its scientific foundation: “This is ultimately about people—the same people who will be engaged and who will benefit from the exercise. The outcomes will guide important health decisions on HIV and other diseases for Lagos and Nigeria” ; reaffirmed the CDC's commitment to providing technical support, stressing that stakeholders must facilitate access for field workers and ensure community acceptance to guarantee credible results.

a4568.speaker: Dr Chioma Ukanwa, Deputy Director of Prevention, NASCP (representing National Coordinator Dr Adebola Bashorun)
a4568.name: Dr Chioma Ukanwa
a4568.title: Deputy Director of Prevention, NASCP (representing National Coordinator Dr Adebola Bashorun)
a4568.speech: Described the AIS as a globally recognised exercise vital to epidemic control: “The survey will reach homes, communities and local governments, providing a true picture of the HIV situation. We need reliable data to make informed decisions and improve healthcare outcomes” ; called on community leaders to sensitise members, emphasising that cooperation with data collectors would determine the success of the survey.

a4568.speaker: Mr Francis Agbo, Director of Research Monitoring and Evaluation, NACA
a4568.name: Mr Francis Agbo
a4568.title: Director of Research Monitoring and Evaluation, NACA
a4568.speech: Said the survey presents an opportunity to track progress towards HIV epidemic control in Lagos: “We have just concluded a similar exercise in Akwa Ibom, and Lagos is the next frontier. The indicators will help us plan for the future.”

a4568.speaker: Dr Williams Nwachukwu, Deputy Director, Department of Surveillance, Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)
a4568.name: Dr Williams Nwachukwu
a4568.title: Deputy Director, Department of Surveillance, Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)
a4568.speech: Assured stakeholders of NCDC's technical support in ensuring quality data collection and analysis: “We are here to ensure that data and samples are properly preserved, tested, and analysed with feedback provided.”

a4568.speaker: Dr Dare Onimode, Project Director, APIN-PHIS3 Project
a4568.name: Dr Dare Onimode
a4568.title: Project Director, APIN-PHIS3 Project
a4568.speech: Described the town hall as another milestone in Nigeria's fight against HIV: “This meeting provides the opportunity to seek your support for the process. The progress made so far is due to the invaluable backing of stakeholders.”

a4568.speaker: Mr Patric Akpan, representative of the Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS in Nigeria (NEPWHAN)
a4568.name: Mr Patric Akpan
a4568.title: representative of the Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS in Nigeria (NEPWHAN)
a4568.speech: Delivering a goodwill message, pledged community support for the survey: “It is essential to generate accurate data because reliable data from Lagos will inform sound policy decisions for Nigeria.”

a4568.speaker: Dr Victoria Egunjobi, Director of Disease Control, Lagos State Ministry of Health
a4568.name: Dr Victoria Egunjobi
a4568.title: Director of Disease Control, Lagos State Ministry of Health
a4568.speech: Underscored the need for community trust and participation to ensure credible outcomes: “Gone are the days when HIV was shrouded in stigma. Today, people living with HIV deserve dignity, respect and universal access to healthcare. This survey is about evaluating progress and closing gaps.”

a4568.speaker: Dr Oladipupo Fisher, Lagos State AIDS Programme Coordinator
a4568.name: Dr Oladipupo Fisher
a4568.title: Lagos State AIDS Programme Coordinator
a4568.speech: Explained in his presentation on the Community Mobilisation and Advocacy Strategy that the ART Impact Survey would rely heavily on grassroots participation to succeed, reiterating that the survey covers 205 randomly selected Enumeration Areas with about 6,150 households and an estimated 11,000 participants and would deploy 30 survey teams supported by mobilisers ; emphasised that community mobilisation was crucial to creating awareness, building trust and encouraging participation: “The mobilisation process will be done in three phases—before, during and after data collection—using strategies such as poster placement, town hall meetings, door-to-door visits, and targeted outreach to selected households” ; noted mobilisers would schedule appointments, respond to questions, monitor perceptions to dispel myths about HIV testing, distribute brochures and ensure households were available ; “Our aim is to saturate the communities with AIS messages, foster understanding of the survey’s purpose, and ensure households cooperate with field workers.”

a4984.speaker: Sethi Steel Factory (company)
a4984.name: Sethi Steel Factory (company)
a4984.speech: says there was no injury besides the death of an employee, Saah Samukai, in the oxygen explosion at the factory.

a4984.speaker: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of Liberia
a4984.name: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of Liberia
a4984.speech: disclosed that Sethi, which enjoys a monopoly on building materials such as steel, zinc, nails, and others, has been operating in the country without a license.

a4984.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel Urey Yarkpawolo, EPA Executive Director
a4984.name: Dr. Emmanuel Urey Yarkpawolo
a4984.title: EPA Executive Director
a4984.speech: told reporters: "This is a serious matter because a Liberian's life has been taken away, so my team at the EPA has come to observe and find out exactly how the accident took place. And we have gathered in our preliminary findings a few safety concerns; there are several things: some are good, and some are bad, and we must take the bad ones very seriously" ; "The first thing, when we heard about the accident, our team came immediately and shut down the factory; another thing, we have observed Sethi Ferro has been operating without a license, and we are going through the investigation for stringent action."

a4984.speaker: Rep. Ivar K. Jones, Electoral District 2, Margibi County (communication to plenary)
a4984.name: Rep. Ivar K. Jones
a4984.title: Electoral District 2, Margibi County (communication to plenary)
a4984.speech: cites Article 8 of the 1986 Constitution, which guarantees just and humane working conditions for all citizens, and stresses that the government must ensure that factories operating in Liberia adhere to strict safety standards: "When people leave their homes in the morning to go to work, their families expect them to return safely. If safety measures are not enforced, and these investors continue to operate without regard for human life, then this is a concern for all of us."

a5201.speaker: Sebastian !Gobs, Khorixas Constituency Councillor
a5201.name: Sebastian !Gobs
a5201.title: Khorixas Constituency Councillor
a5201.speech: Confirmed in an interview with nbc News that, as drought persists across the Kunene Region, Khorixas' constituency office is challenged by transport to deliver much-needed food aid to rural residents.

a5201.speaker: Caretaker for displaced people at the Katutura Youth Complex (unnamed)
a5201.name: Caretaker for displaced people at the Katutura Youth Complex (unnamed)
a5201.speech: Has appealed to good Samaritans, including the government, to come to the aid of the homeless.

a5281.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5281.name: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a5281.title: researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5281.speech: Said that generally speaking the United States' interest in Africa remains minimal relative to the stakes and expectations, and that whatever the Americans choose there should not be any major revolution in US Africa policy, which has placed its priorities elsewhere since the end of the Cold War; however, one can expect more engagement from the Democrat Kamala Harris, who should remain in the same line as Joe Biden, which contrasts with Donald Trump, during whose first term political interest in Africa was almost non-existent, even though in 2018 he launched his economic initiative Prosper Africa.

a5281.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5281.name: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a5281.title: researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5281.speech: Said the most important thing will be AGOA, whose renewal will have to be decided in 2025, and that AGOA remains first and foremost a tool of coercive economic diplomacy (economic statecraft), since African countries that do not align with the American vision of human rights and democracy can be removed from it, as with Rwanda in 2018 and Niger and Uganda in 2023, a policy that should continue ; said the 2022 US-Africa Summit restored the American will to invest more in Africa with the promise of 55 billion dollars, and that Kamala Harris should follow the same line ; noted the United States keeps an eye on Chinese expansion in Africa and wants to compete with Beijing through investments in strategic infrastructure such as Angola's Lobito Corridor, and that the same strategy of containing China can be expected with Donald Trump, for whom competition with China is an obsession.

a5281.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5281.name: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a5281.title: researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5281.speech: Said that for the moment the security component of American policy in Africa remains relegated to the background in the American campaign, but that the fight against terrorism still retains a certain importance for Washington; the United States has particular worries regarding its military presence in the Sahel and competition from Russia, as American troops were forced to leave Niger and the challenge now is to remain in the region, with Cote d'Ivoire and Benin possible hosts in an increasingly hostile West African climate; Russia has gained legitimacy through its presence in Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso via its African Corps, and the new administration, whether under Trump or Harris, will have to have geopolitical answers.

a5281.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5281.name: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a5281.title: researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5281.speech: Said Trump, who pays less attention to Africa, should probably be less demanding about governance or human rights, but that on humanitarian aid Trump, who has a mercantilist perception of international relations, had wanted to cut several funding streams during his first term - a subject that could return to the table of Congress and call into question certain projects in Africa, and the investments announced at the last US-Africa Summit could also be reviewed by a Trump administration ; added that some Africans could prefer the Republican because Kamala Harris could tie American aid and investment more closely to the promotion or decriminalisation of homosexuality in African countries, a fundamental civilisational divergence that will not exist with Trump, and that Harris should be more demanding on questions of democracy and respect for human rights.

a5281.speaker: Kamala Harris, US Vice-President
a5281.name: Kamala Harris
a5281.title: US Vice-President
a5281.speech: During her tour of Africa in March 2023, notably in Ghana, Zambia and Tanzania, said she was "enthusiastic" about the future of Africa and about American-African cooperation, and announced support for digitalisation and innovation in Africa.

a5287.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a5287.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a5287.speech: Says the rise in pregnancy and early marriage as well as HIV infections among adolescent girls is a cause for concern.

a5287.speaker: Dr Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a5287.name: Dr Kalumbi Shangula
a5287.title: Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a5287.speech: Revealed the dilemma of teenage pregnancies at the handover of reproductive health kits and contraceptives worth N$200 million, noting the rate of teenage pregnancies nationally stands at 14.95%, translating to more than 15 thousand pregnancies per year: "Our young people, especially young women, deserve to be educated and empowered to protect themselves and to make the right choices regarding reproduction at all times. It is equally important that young men must be instilled with the understanding that they should respect the wishes and rights of women. This must become the norm in our society."

a5287.speaker: Noriaki Sadamoto, Charge d'Affaires at the Japanese Embassy
a5287.name: Noriaki Sadamoto
a5287.title: Charge d'Affaires at the Japanese Embassy
a5287.speech: "For the international community to strengthen cooperation in order to overcome the crises together and to promote human security for all, this is the basis of Japanese development assistance. It aims to advance nation building through empowerment and protection of individuals to live happily and in dignity."

a5287.speaker: Government of Japan
a5287.name: Government of Japan
a5287.speech: Has also committed to assisting Namibia in its efforts to deliver effective services.

a5287.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a5287.name: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a5287.speech: Pledged to continue supporting Namibia in the area of family planning.

a5434.speaker: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana
a5434.name: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo
a5434.title: President of Ghana
a5434.speech: Made a compelling case for increased Chinese investment in Ghana, emphasizing the longstanding relationship between Ghana and China as well as the tremendous investment opportunities Ghana offers in sectors ranging from manufacturing to agriculture and green energy ; opened his address with a Chinese proverb, “If you want to walk far, walk with someone,” symbolizing Ghana’s desire to walk hand-in-hand with China on the path to long-term economic progress ; highlighted Ghana’s determination to learn from China’s success story and its commitment to deepening ties with China’s business community to ensure mutual prosperity.

a5434.speaker: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana
a5434.name: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo
a5434.title: President of Ghana
a5434.speech: Emphasized the strong trade relations between Ghana and China, noting that China has been Ghana’s largest trading partner since 2015 and that in 2023 trade between the two nations reached $9.23 billion ; commended Chinese companies for their continued investment in key sectors such as construction, energy, agriculture, and ICT, and attributed China’s growing presence in Ghana to the West African country’s stability, security, and welcoming investment environment.

a5434.speaker: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana
a5434.name: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo
a5434.title: President of Ghana
a5434.speech: Reflecting on the global challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, pointed out that these events have exposed structural weaknesses across Africa ; urged the business community to partner with Ghana to create resilient, climate-conscious, and diversified economies that can withstand future global shocks, saying international cooperation will be essential in building economies that thrive despite global disruptions.

a5434.speaker: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana
a5434.name: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo
a5434.title: President of Ghana
a5434.speech: Highlighted Ghana’s progress under his administration, citing his government’s efforts to foster a business-friendly environment since assuming office in 2017 ; noted that Ghana’s economy grew rapidly between 2017 and 2020, with an average annual GDP growth rate of 7% ; expressed optimism that, despite the economic setbacks caused by the pandemic and geopolitical challenges, Ghana is once again on a path of robust economic growth.

a5434.speaker: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana
a5434.name: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo
a5434.title: President of Ghana
a5434.speech: Highlighted his government’s ambitious Ghana CARES ‘Obaatampa’ Programme, a comprehensive economic revitalization plan aimed at addressing the challenges caused by the pandemic, and invited Chinese businesses to contribute to this effort, emphasizing the importance of partnerships in rebuilding the Ghanaian economy ; showcased a range of government programs designed to boost industrialization and economic development, including the “Planting for Food and Jobs” initiative, the development of Ghana’s nascent automotive sector, and efforts to build integrated bauxite and iron industries, which he explained are part of Ghana’s broader strategy to transition from an exporter of raw materials to a value-added, industrialized economy.

a5434.speaker: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana
a5434.name: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo
a5434.title: President of Ghana
a5434.speech: Spoke about Ghana’s unique position as the host of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat in Accra, pointing out that the continental trade agreement offers immense opportunities for businesses to access African markets: “We are leveraging the AfCFTA to become a new commercial capital of Africa.”

a5434.speaker: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana
a5434.name: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo
a5434.title: President of Ghana
a5434.speech: Reiterated in closing that Ghana is an ideal destination for Chinese investment, with a stable regulatory environment, favorable fiscal policies, and abundant natural resources, and urged Chinese investors to seize the moment, stressing that Ghana’s doors are open and its markets are ready to support meaningful partnerships ; “Let us seize this moment to forge stronger ties, build lasting partnerships, and create shared prosperity for the people of Ghana and China.”

a5490.speaker: Namibian Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) and Namibia Press Agency (NAMPA)
a5490.name: Namibian Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) and Namibia Press Agency (NAMPA)
a5490.speech: Have reaffirmed their longstanding partnership, committing to deepen cooperation in content sharing, resource utilisation and newsroom collaboration.

a5490.speaker: Telecom Namibia
a5490.name: Telecom Namibia
a5490.speech: Has warned that the escalating copper theft is threatening critical telecommunications infrastructure and putting lives at risk, calling for stronger law enforcement and government intervention.

a5490.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Minister of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
a5490.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a5490.title: Minister of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
a5490.speech: Revealed during a Cabinet Committee Briefing on Friday that Namibia's visa-on-arrival system has generated more than N$413 million in revenue in less than 12 months.

a5490.speaker: Organisers of Namibia's 36th Independence Day celebrations in the Kunene Region
a5490.name: Organisers of Namibia's 36th Independence Day celebrations in the Kunene Region
a5490.speech: Expressed confidence that the town of Khorixas is ready to host the regional event scheduled for March 21, 2026.

a5490.speaker: Yarukeekuro Steven Ndorokaze, NamRA's Chief of Strategic Communications, Stakeholder Engagement, and Taxpayer Education
a5490.name: Yarukeekuro Steven Ndorokaze
a5490.title: NamRA's Chief of Strategic Communications, Stakeholder Engagement, and Taxpayer Education
a5490.speech: Described the N$90 billion owed to the Namibia Revenue Agency by taxpayers as a historic debt.

a5490.speaker: Pan African Women's Organisation (PAWO)
a5490.name: Pan African Women's Organisation (PAWO)
a5490.speech: Has strongly condemned the United States government's latest sanctions against Cuba, describing it as a deliberate attempt to destabilise Cuba.

a5562.speaker: Dr Stanford Ndibalema, Assistant Director of Veterinary Services at the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries
a5562.name: Dr Stanford Ndibalema
a5562.title: Assistant Director of Veterinary Services at the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries
a5562.speech: Said there is need for collaboration in combating rabies: "The partnership between USAID and the Tanzanian government is crucial in our fight against rabies." He added that by working together, the government of Tanzania and USAID can ensure the communities are educated about the risks of rabies and properly empowered to take proactive steps in protecting themselves and their pets.

a5562.speaker: Dr Stanford Ndibalema, Assistant Director of Veterinary Services at the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries
a5562.name: Dr Stanford Ndibalema
a5562.title: Assistant Director of Veterinary Services at the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries
a5562.speech: Underscored the critical need for vaccination and community awareness campaigns: "Every vaccinated dog is a step toward to having a rabies-free community."

a5562.speaker: Revina John, a mother of three from Mwanza
a5562.name: Revina John
a5562.title: a mother of three from Mwanza
a5562.speech: "Before the campaign, I had no idea how dangerous rabies could be." She added: "After we learnt about the importance of vaccinating our dogs, we took immediate action. Now, I feel much safer allowing my children to play outside."

a5734.speaker: Chris Puta, MTF Southern Africa Academy director
a5734.name: Chris Puta
a5734.title: MTF Southern Africa Academy director
a5734.speech: “We promote women filmmakers in numbers and in terms of creative support. Women students consistently make up around 50% of our cohort intake. But I believe what is most important is that they are given license to express themselves as writers, directors and producers. This is how women’s voices enter the mainstream.”

a5734.speaker: Atinuke Babatunde, MTF West Africa Academy Director
a5734.name: Atinuke Babatunde
a5734.title: MTF West Africa Academy Director
a5734.speech: “We believe in empowering women in the film industry through training, mentorship, and opportunities. We give them all the skills they require to make a statement in the industry. And that is exactly what they are doing.”

a5734.speaker: Victoria Goro, MTF Academy East Director
a5734.name: Victoria Goro
a5734.title: MTF Academy East Director
a5734.speech: “MTF is committed to seeing women pursue careers in film and TV. Besides upskilling young women filmmakers, we believe a highly effective way to encourage girls and young women to get into film is to inspire them by seeing great work by young women.”

a5734.speaker: Serena Mmifinyane, former MTF student, creative director at N&M Productions and founder of the Women in Film Guild Botswana
a5734.name: Serena Mmifinyane
a5734.title: former MTF student, creative director at N&M Productions and founder of the Women in Film Guild Botswana
a5734.speech: “I am proud of what I have been able to achieve in the film sector. But the hundreds of other young women who have come through MTF Academies have all made great strides in our industry. Their achievements exemplify the talent and drive of Africa’s women filmmakers, and how training can be a catalyst to accelerate gender empowerment across our continent.”

a5847.speaker: Ahmed Baffoe, Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Athletics Association (GAA)
a5847.name: Ahmed Baffoe
a5847.title: Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Athletics Association (GAA)
a5847.speech: Announced plans to put Ghanaian athletes based in the United States into training camps ahead of the World Athletics Championship in September, emphasising the importance of keeping athletes active during the off-season and noting that the US outdoor season ends in May: "We have a little bit of an issue. Athletes based in the U.S., right after the outdoor competition which ends in May, wouldn't have competitions until September. So between May and September, what do we do for these athletes? We want to try and put them in training camps." ; proposed sending them to Europe: "There are a lot of competitions coming up in Europe. We can also help by putting them in these training camps and competitions so that it would fine-tune their performance. By the time they hit September, they'll be at top level and perform well. Trust me, if we continue that way, we'll win laurels at the World Championship in Tokyo."

a5847.speaker: Ahmed Baffoe, Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Athletics Association (GAA)
a5847.name: Ahmed Baffoe
a5847.title: Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Athletics Association (GAA)
a5847.speech: Expressed optimism that more Ghanaian athletes, particularly those based abroad, will qualify for individual events in addition to the relays: "What we are hoping for is to get more athletes to qualify for the individual races - that is the 100m, 200m, 400m, and even the long-distance events. We hope that the athletes who live abroad are going to improve their performances."

a5847.speaker: Ahmed Baffoe, Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Athletics Association (GAA)
a5847.name: Ahmed Baffoe
a5847.title: Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Athletics Association (GAA)
a5847.speech: Pointed out that while Ghana's relay team has already qualified, there are other strong contenders: "Remember that the quartet that qualified for the World Cup are not the only strong sprinters we have. There are others such as Saminu, Azamati, and Botsio who were not able to make it for the competition."

a6282.speaker: Organisers of the 19th National Crafts Fair of Benin (Snab), press conference at the supervising ministry
a6282.name: Organisers of the 19th National Crafts Fair of Benin (Snab)
a6282.title: press conference at the supervising ministry
a6282.speech: Announced that the fair will run for ten days, from 22 to 31 August, and unveiled the main features of the biggest craft event in Benin.

a6282.speaker: Organisers of the 19th National Crafts Fair of Benin (Snab)
a6282.name: Organisers of the 19th National Crafts Fair of Benin (Snab)
a6282.speech: Affirm that this 19th edition must leave a lasting mark: “Labelling and certification are not a luxury, but a key to propelling Beninese crafts onto the big markets, protecting our heritage and improving the incomes of our artisans. Investing in quality is investing in the future.”

a6282.speaker: Organisers of the 19th National Crafts Fair of Benin (Snab)
a6282.name: Organisers of the 19th National Crafts Fair of Benin (Snab)
a6282.speech: “For good deals, we exhibit and sell on site and to order. Many are already digitalised — catalogues, contacts and follow-up via messaging, which makes repeat purchases easier.”

a6282.speaker: Cyr Davodoun, acting Secretary General of the Chamber of Trades and Crafts
a6282.name: Cyr Davodoun
a6282.title: acting Secretary General of the Chamber of Trades and Crafts
a6282.speech: “We guarantee that you will find truly very interesting products. And do not miss this opportunity to obtain authentically Beninese products.”

a6282.speaker: Sotima Michel Yotto, Deputy Chief of Staff to the Minister of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Employment Promotion
a6282.name: Sotima Michel Yotto
a6282.title: Deputy Chief of Staff to the Minister of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Employment Promotion
a6282.speech: Maintains that the fair intends to give momentum to creators.

a6282.speaker: Cossi Clétus Nestor Guézo, Director General of the Crafts Development Fund (Fonds de développement de l'artisanat)
a6282.name: Cossi Clétus Nestor Guézo
a6282.title: Director General of the Crafts Development Fund (Fonds de développement de l'artisanat)
a6282.speech: “Our objective is to turn the public's emotion into an order, and the order into a job” ; “Come and see how we transform material into beauty and an idea into a trade. Leave with a piece that has a story, a gift for the new school year, or a craftsman's contract that will give someone work tomorrow.”

a6411.speaker: National Bureau of Statistics (Nigeria)
a6411.name: National Bureau of Statistics (Nigeria)
a6411.speech: According to the National Bureau of Statistics, the herbs and spice market in Nigeria is valued at over N100 billion, with ginger being the most valuable spice.

a6538.speaker: USAID Nigeria-State Accountability, Transparency, and Effectiveness (‘State2State’) Activity
a6538.name: USAID Nigeria-State Accountability
a6538.title: Transparency, and Effectiveness (‘State2State’) Activity
a6538.speech: Has called on the States in Nigeria to prioritise sustainable reforms to promote good governance in Nigeria; made the call at the National Conference for State Transformation Committees (STCs) held in Abuja.

a6538.speaker: Chris Okeke, Senior Governance Advisor of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO)
a6538.name: Chris Okeke
a6538.title: Senior Governance Advisor of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO)
a6538.speech: Tasked States across the country to embrace good practices and approaches to sustain reforms beyond programme support, political transitions and changes to office holders; urged states to focus attention on inclusivity, youth empowerment and public service reforms to improve productivity in governance; underscored the need for public sector reforms that would streamline bureaucratic procedures and improve transparency and accountability in governance systems; pointed out the indispensable role of the civil service in driving sustainable reforms: “The important thing for the long-term sustenance of reforms is the issue of bureaucracy and how the civil service can contribute to the sustainability of reforms, including reforms such as public financial management systems, public service reforms, empowerment and accountability. During our discussion, we highlighted the critical point with regard to the suitability of the public service structure. We questioned whether it was fit for purpose, considering the functions and human skills within the civil service. Additionally, we examined how effective the planning and preparation of key talents were, as well as the issue of succession gaps within the civil service.” ; stressed the need for state governments to focus on developing local capacity to effectively manage the resources that have already been provided.

a6538.speaker: Dr. Uzochukwu Amakom, Senior Public Financial Management Expert
a6538.name: Dr. Uzochukwu Amakom
a6538.title: Senior Public Financial Management Expert
a6538.speech: Emphasised the need for institutions to adopt good practices that conform to global standards to achieve their set goals and objectives: “Whether you are doing reforms or not, the end point is how does it affect service delivery? It is not creating new institutions that matter, it is the result. This is what reforms entail. If you do good realistic revenue forecasting, you embrace good cash planning and expenditure prioritisation, there will be good results.” ; urged states to insist on planning realistic budgets and revenue: “It is vital for states to prioritise accountability and transparency while planning their budgets to ensure that funds are allocated to the areas that need them the most.”

a6697.speaker: HIV response researchers
a6697.name: HIV response researchers
a6697.speech: Sounded the alarm over recent global funding cuts, saying they have severely disrupted efforts to combat HIV, threatening life-saving research, prevention and treatment ; during the conference the experts revealed predictive modelling and real-world data from Africa and Latin America, indicating rising HIV acquisitions, stalled treatment and fragile health systems.

a6697.speaker: Dr Beatriz Grinsztejn, IAS (International Aids Society) president
a6697.name: Dr Beatriz Grinsztejn
a6697.title: IAS (International Aids Society) president
a6697.speech: Said that, on one hand, the world is witnessing extraordinary scientific breakthroughs that could transform prevention and treatment and "even bring us closer to a cure" ; "On the other hand, these very advances are under threat from massive funding cuts that risk stalling clinical trials, slowing our progress and jeopardising the achievements we've fought so hard to attain."

a6697.speaker: Professor Kenneth Ngure, IAS president-elect
a6697.name: Professor Kenneth Ngure
a6697.title: IAS president-elect
a6697.speech: Said that the sudden cuts to United States funding, announced earlier this year, have been "deeply felt" across the African continent by millions of people who rely on HIV prevention, testing and treatment services.

a6697.speaker: Dr Jack Stone, Associate Professor in Infectious Disease Mathematical Modelling, University of Bristol (lead author, preprint modelling study)
a6697.name: Dr Jack Stone
a6697.title: Associate Professor in Infectious Disease Mathematical Modelling, University of Bristol (lead author, preprint modelling study)
a6697.speech: HIV incidence and related deaths are expected to rise significantly in sub-Saharan Africa due to disruptions in funding for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) under Pepfar. The study suggests that the January 2025 pause could result in approximately 6,671 additional HIV acquisitions over one year, and a further 3,617 cases over the subsequent five years; more than 2,900 of these additional cases are projected to occur among gay and bisexual men who have sex with men, while over 2,000 are expected among female sex workers ; "It is crucial that funding is secured to continue and expand PrEP services in sub-Saharan Africa."

a6697.speaker: Zackie Achmat, founder of the Treatment Action Campaign and member of the Global HIV Treatment Coalition
a6697.name: Zackie Achmat
a6697.title: founder of the Treatment Action Campaign and member of the Global HIV Treatment Coalition
a6697.speech: Issued a call to action on the urgent need for debt refinancing to protect the HIV response in low- and middle-income countries: "You can't end the Aids pandemic while African nations must choose between paying creditors and saving lives. As someone who has lived with HIV for more than half my life, I have seen the cost of political inaction." ; "We fought for treatment when the world said it was impossible. Now, the convergence of crushing debt and funding cuts threatens everything we've built. We need urgent debt restructuring so African countries can invest in saving lives instead of servicing debt."

a6833.speaker: Matias Nyazi (Njazi), lead farmer, Chipakuza village, Chikwawa
a6833.name: Matias Nyazi (Njazi)
a6833.title: lead farmer, Chipakuza village, Chikwawa
a6833.speech: Recalls the prolonged dry spell scorching maturing crops that were expected to end hunger caused by the devastating floods: “We looked at the data and noticed that hunger was the common problem, so we agreed to embrace irrigation farming.”

a6833.speaker: Matias Nyazi (Njazi), lead farmer, Chipakuza village, Chikwawa
a6833.name: Matias Nyazi (Njazi)
a6833.title: lead farmer, Chipakuza village, Chikwawa
a6833.speech: “The cost of irrigation is much lower than buying 50 kilogrammes of maize at K45 000. At the current price, I need K450 000 for 10 bags.” ; on the vegetables he also grows, which earn him at least K10 000 a week: “I use the money to meet the daily needs of my family and boost my farming business.”

a6833.speaker: Group village head (GVH) Chipakuza, traditional leader
a6833.name: Group village head (GVH) Chipakuza
a6833.title: traditional leader
a6833.speech: According to GVH Chipakuza, the findings have ranked food insecurity as a major concern for 92 percent of the households in the area: “Based on the reports, as community leaders, we had to think of what we can do to end hunger. We met and identified this irrigated piece of land for communal use to sustain our families.” ; on using the data to persuade development partners who constructed a dyke to prevent flooding: “We use the same data to convince well-wishers to help us.”

a6833.speaker: Evelyn Jonasi, Area Development Committee (ADC) vice-chairperson
a6833.name: Evelyn Jonasi
a6833.title: Area Development Committee (ADC) vice-chairperson
a6833.speech: Says the RFMS has made decision-making simple: “When the ADC wants to present issues to the council or lobby for project funding, we use this data as our backing. With data, it has really become easy for the council and other development partners to assist our communities.”

a6833.speaker: World Bank
a6833.name: World Bank
a6833.speech: Rates RFMS highly as a cost-effective and reliable tool for capturing real-time data relating to poverty and climate change.

a7036.speaker: John Kirby, spokesman for the White House National Security Council
a7036.name: John Kirby
a7036.title: spokesman for the White House National Security Council
a7036.speech: “A ceasefire at this stage would only benefit Hamas,” he told the press on Tuesday, also warning that the situation was going to get even worse for civilians ; while Washington opposes a full ceasefire, sporadic halts in the fighting in order to facilitate the delivery of aid to the Gaza Strip should be “considered,” he qualified ; “We want to see protective measures for civilians. Now, pauses in operations are a tool, a tactic, that can achieve that for a temporary period (...) but that is not the same thing as a ceasefire.”

a7036.speaker: Joe Biden, President of the United States
a7036.name: Joe Biden
a7036.title: President of the United States
a7036.speech: Said on Tuesday that humanitarian aid was not arriving fast enough in the Gaza Strip; the delivery is “not fast enough,” he said when questioned by the press at the White House.

a7036.speaker: Antonio Guterres, United Nations Secretary-General
a7036.name: Antonio Guterres
a7036.title: United Nations Secretary-General
a7036.speech: Called for an “immediate humanitarian ceasefire” between Israel and Hamas: “To ease this immense suffering, to make the distribution of aid safer, and to facilitate the release of the hostages, I repeat my call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire,” while denouncing “clear violations” of humanitarian law in Gaza.

a7036.speaker: Eli Cohen, Israeli Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7036.name: Eli Cohen
a7036.title: Israeli Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7036.speech: “Mr Secretary-General, what world are you living in,” he said before cancelling his meeting with Antonio Guterres ; “How can you conclude a ceasefire agreement with someone who has sworn to kill and destroy your very existence.”

a7036.speaker: Hamas Health Ministry
a7036.name: Hamas Health Ministry
a7036.speech: States that 5,791 people have been killed since 7 October and the beginning of the Israeli strikes on the Gaza Strip.

a7162.speaker: The New York Times (citing lists provided to officials and humanitarian workers)
a7162.name: The New York Times (citing lists provided to officials and humanitarian workers)
a7162.speech: Reported that the administration of American President Donald Trump has cut aid programmes for several countries where it had initially promised to maintain its support; according to these lists, the United States will cease financing programmes in Afghanistan, Iraq, Jordan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Lebanon, Madagascar, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Syria, Somalia, Chad and Yemen.

a7162.speaker: Reuters (citing sources)
a7162.name: Reuters (citing sources)
a7162.speech: Reported on 9 April that the White House later decided to restore payments under the World Food Programme (WFP) in Lebanon, Syria, Somalia, Jordan, Iraq and Ecuador.

a7162.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a7162.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a7162.speech: Estimates that Washington's refusal to provide aid will have the greatest impact in Afghanistan, where about 2 million people, including 400,000 children, depend on the food, and that the population of Yemen will also suffer, where 2.4 million people receive food under humanitarian programmes.

a7162.speaker: USAID staff speaking to the NYT (anonymous)
a7162.name: USAID staff speaking to the NYT (anonymous)
a7162.speech: Stressed that they often learn of the end of the next programme directly from the humanitarian organisations that stop receiving funds.

a7162.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (previously appointed acting head of USAID)
a7162.name: Marco Rubio
a7162.title: US Secretary of State (previously appointed acting head of USAID)
a7162.speech: Announced on 10 March that the American government, at the conclusion of a six-week audit, had officially ended 83% of the agency's programmes; according to him, under the 5,200 contracts that were cancelled, tens of billions of dollars had been spent not in the interests of the United States, and in some cases to their detriment.

a7389.speaker: Albert Chimbindi, Zimbabwean permanent secretary for Foreign Affairs and International Trade
a7389.name: Albert Chimbindi
a7389.title: Zimbabwean permanent secretary for Foreign Affairs and International Trade
a7389.speech: Speaking at the close of the session, hailed the meeting as notably productive, adding that it was conducted in a spirit of camaraderie befitting the excellent state of relations between the two neighbouring countries; expressed gratitude to his Zambian counterpart Etambuyu Gundersen, to the Zimbabwean ambassador to Zambia Charity Charamba, and to the Zambian charge d'affaires to Zimbabwe Nabulanga Natlasha; commended the tireless work of the sectoral committees and officials; said the outcomes of the review serve as a roadmap to strengthen both bilateral and multilateral relations.

a7389.speaker: Albert Chimbindi, Zimbabwean permanent secretary for Foreign Affairs and International Trade
a7389.name: Albert Chimbindi
a7389.title: Zimbabwean permanent secretary for Foreign Affairs and International Trade
a7389.speech: "In light of the unprecedented geopolitical developments, rising tariffs, and the decline in foreign aid that are disrupting trade and investment flows across the SADC region, it is in our national interests to optimise opportunities for mutual benefit." ; Noted that both countries had set clear benchmarks and targets to ensure accountability to their principals, stressing the need for resilience and a united voice in advancing the development priorities of the Southern African region and the continent at large.

a7389.speaker: Senior officials from Zimbabwe and Zambia
a7389.name: Senior officials from Zimbabwe and Zambia
a7389.speech: Reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral ties across key sectors at the conclusion of the Mid-Term Review of the 18th Session of the Zimbabwe-Zambia Joint Permanent Commission on Cooperation.

a7399.speaker: Ministry in charge of the Promotion of Women, Children and the Family of Mali
a7399.name: Ministry in charge of the Promotion of Women
a7399.title: Children and the Family of Mali
a7399.speech: Intends to take up the challenge of girls' schooling, placing a particular stamp on scientific fields, as illustrated by the national theme of the day, “The refoundation of education through the support of girls in scientific fields.”

a7399.speaker: Korotoum Diarra, Country Director of Plan International Mali
a7399.name: Korotoum Diarra
a7399.title: Country Director of Plan International Mali
a7399.speech: In her remarks, insisted on the need to promote children's rights and equality for girls, who are particularly victims of violence of all kinds, notably in countries in conflict; said that is why Plan International has set itself objectives to bring out girls' capacities as leaders, while underlining the need to undertake specific efforts for their long-term empowerment, to create a solidarity network for participating girls and young women, and to ensure visibility in the press and on social networks of the issues they defend; issued an appeal to the government and to socio-political actors for joint action in favour of respect for children's rights and equal opportunities for girls — halting and condemning all grave violence against children in conflicts, supporting safe and inclusive education for children and young people, and targeting humanitarian aid for children's access to food, water and shelter.

a7399.speaker: Oumou Yanogo, Regional Director for West and Central Africa of Plan International
a7399.name: Oumou Yanogo
a7399.title: Regional Director for West and Central Africa of Plan International
a7399.speech: Expressed her pride in the organisation of the Day dedicated to the girl child; congratulated the commitment of Plan International, which places the young girl at the centre of its actions, including education and health, for her development.

a7399.speaker: Jackson Acha Atam, outgoing country director / Resident Representative of Plan International Mali
a7399.name: Jackson Acha Atam
a7399.title: outgoing country director / Resident Representative of Plan International Mali
a7399.speech: Recalled the context of the celebration of the Day dedicated to the girl child, which, according to him, points to the particular nature of women's needs; said he believes in women's capacity to acquire the skills and practise the same trades as men; considers that the young girl needs particular support so that she may enjoy all her rights, which, he specifies, requires raising parents' awareness of the consequences of early marriage and of girls dropping out of school.

a7448.speaker: Civil society campaigners (Kenya)
a7448.name: Civil society campaigners (Kenya)
a7448.speech: Are renewing the fight against plastic bags in Kenya, arguing that they pose a real threat to the health of citizens.

a7448.speaker: James Wakibia, environmentalist
a7448.name: James Wakibia
a7448.title: environmentalist
a7448.speech: "We held a meeting with the Chief Officer of Environment, Richard Rop, who promised that the government would use 52-million Kenyan shillings (R7.8-million) to control the garbage, with half of that amount going into fencing the dumpsite. Three years down the line, nothing has happened," he added.

a7448.speaker: Richard Rop, Chief Officer of Environment
a7448.name: Richard Rop
a7448.title: Chief Officer of Environment
a7448.speech: Promised that the government would use 52-million Kenyan shillings to control the garbage, with half of that amount going into fencing the dumpsite.

a7448.speaker: James Wakibia, environmentalist
a7448.name: James Wakibia
a7448.title: environmentalist
a7448.speech: Analysed the type of garbage trashed in the facility, and realised that it was mostly plastic bags. "I knew if I had to solve the crisis I needed to deal with the small plastic paper bags, popularly known as the single use bags, that flew everywhere," he said; believes the garbage collected in Lake Nakuru is responsible for the rise in water levels in the Lake, which is threatening local homes and livelihoods.

a7448.speaker: Report on Lake Nakuru garbage
a7448.name: Report on Lake Nakuru garbage
a7448.speech: A report saying that 20 thousand tonnes of garbage are collected in Lake Nakuru, one of Kenya's largest water sources, every year.

a7448.speaker: James Wakibia, environmentalist
a7448.name: James Wakibia
a7448.title: environmentalist
a7448.speech: "Nairobi County had admitted that 70 percent of the garbage collected was [plastic] bags. Lamu, Malindi and Kisii and had also indicated that they would deal with the issue," he said.

a7448.speaker: James Wakibia, environmentalist
a7448.name: James Wakibia
a7448.title: environmentalist
a7448.speech: Believes that businesses can play a vital role in fixing the problem. "Supermarkets are the biggest producers of plastics, with an estimated one million bags behind distributed in the country annually. Unfortunately they do not follow up on where the bags end up and hence they are the biggest culprits in the environmental degradation. They should be the ones on the forefront in creating awareness and running environmental campaigns," he said, proposing that supermarkets introduce customer reward points for people who use recyclable bags instead.

a7448.speaker: Githinji Kinyanjui, managing director of Cocorico Investment, a polythene manufacturing firm in Nairobi
a7448.name: Githinji Kinyanjui
a7448.title: managing director of Cocorico Investment, a polythene manufacturing firm in Nairobi
a7448.speech: Challenged the government to come up with a better way of cleaning up the plastic bags mess. "There should be separate bags for different garbage in the homes. Our challenge is when we mix bags and other dirty garbage. We actually have a shortage of clean polythene bags for recycling," says Kinyanjui. He said it is impossible to ban the bags, saying that the high demand for them is market driven.

a7448.speaker: Susan Kihika, Nakuru County Speaker
a7448.name: Susan Kihika
a7448.title: Nakuru County Speaker
a7448.speech: Called for the enforcement of the law passed in 2007 that would see the total eradication of small plastic bags in the country. "When we control plastic bags menace we immediately deal with issues like water borne diseases including cholera and dysentery which are basically as a result of blocked and clogged drainage in the county," said Kihika.

a7448.speaker: Emily Kimani, environmentalist
a7448.name: Emily Kimani
a7448.title: environmentalist
a7448.speech: Said that the easiest way to curb the menace was to create a regulation to bar their manufacture. "Currently we do not have better mechanisms to control their spread in the country and the only way to do so is to completely stop their manufacture," she said.

a7448.speaker: Abdi Hassan Guyo, Nairobi County Assembly representative
a7448.name: Abdi Hassan Guyo
a7448.title: Nairobi County Assembly representative
a7448.speech: Lodged the Nairobi City County Plastic Carry Bags Control Bill (2014), which seeks to ban recycled, nonbiodegradable plastic bags and containers from virgin plastic less than 30 microns thick and 20cm by 30cm in size.
